docs.text: DatasetSpec is the reviewed, executable generation contract. It contains: entities, fields, types, nullability, and row counts; primary keys and relationships; distributions and constraints; privacy annotations; structured business rules; generation and validation settings and schema version. Infer a spec: test-data-agent infer-spec out/profile.json \ --count 100 \ --output out/dataset_spec.yaml Review the spec before generation. Inferred relationships and constraints are candidates, not unquestionable facts.
docs.title: DatasetSpec

docs.text: Generation reads the specification, not source rows: test-data-agent generate out/dataset_spec.yaml \ --seed 12345 \ --format csv \ --output out/generated The seed belongs to the generation request and is recorded in the effective spec and manifest.
docs.title: Generation

docs.text: test-data-agent validate out/dataset_spec.yaml out/generated \ --output out/generated/validation_report.json Validation is deterministic Python code. An AI client may plan or summarize the workflow, but it is not the only validator.
docs.title: Validation

docs.text: Newly constructed DatasetSpec files use schema_version: "1.1" ; version 1.0 remains supported, and serialized files without a version load as 1.0 for compatibility. Exact DECIMAL fields require 1.1 . Keep the schema version, package version, spec_sha256 , business_validation.rules_sha256 , and seed with any dataset that must be reproduced later. The complete field reference is in DatasetSpec .
docs.title: Versioning

docs.text: A reviewed date_range or datetime_range supplies sampling bounds. Missing endpoints use 2020-01-01 and 2025-01-01. Supply both ordered endpoints for an earlier or later period: a partial bound that reverses the effective interval now rejects with a recovery hint. Generation keeps previous output artifacts unchanged on this failure. Datetime sampling retains its whole-second offset policy and the lower endpoint's microseconds. Very long fractional intervals use integer duration arithmetic to stay within the maximum. Range endpoints alone do not establish monthly or other calendar granularity; source-period fidelity remains unmeasured.
docs.title: Date and time bounds

docs.text: Relational Synthesis Contract ¶ English · Русский Relational synthesis preserves reviewed, executable structure. It does not reconstruct source rows, identifiers, totals, or rare values. Generated Identifier Domains ¶ Within one dataset specification, identifier fields have separate deterministic domains, assigned by sorted entity/field names. Integer domains use disjoint sequences; strings encode the same generated sequence with a synthetic prefix, not source identifiers or entity labels. Declared relationships subsequently assign generated parent keys to child fields in dependency order for acyclic graphs. Cyclic components retain legacy input-order reconciliation; all resulting relationships must pass validation before publication. Reordering entities or fields does not change domain numbering or initial non-null identifier values at a given row position, before relationships and constraints are applied. Final FK assignments may change with null masks. Nullable-field masks still consume order-dependent randomness: changing field/entity order may change which rows are null. Exact replay requires the same ordered specification. Replay requires the same specification, seed and algorithm version. Adding or removing identifier fields can change the domain numbering and generated values. This is not a persistent mapping across independently generated datasets. The upcoming 1.6 candidate changes identifier values and their string format; regenerate fixtures rather than relying on the old row-counter equality. Evidence-Bounded Synthesis ¶ The system does not magically discover the complete domain model from a schema or a sample. It records bounded observations, keeps their provenance, and turns unverified conclusions into hypotheses that require review. The conceptual pipeline is: SourceBundle schema + constraints + examples ↓ EvidenceProfile safe observations + provenance ↓ SemanticHypotheses candidate relationships and rules ↓ human review ↓ ReviewedDatasetSpec executable generation contract These artifacts have deliberately different authority: Artifact Meaning Generation authority SourceBundle Input schema, constraints, examples, and sampling metadata None EvidenceProfile Safe observations supported by bounded evidence None SemanticHypothesis Deterministic or AI-proposed relationship/rule None until reviewed ReviewedDatasetSpec Explicitly accepted and executable contract Yes Provenance And Confidence ¶ Every non-declared relationship, distribution, or business rule should retain an evidence envelope containing, where applicable: origin : declared , observed , or inferred ; status : candidate , reviewed , accepted , or rejected ; confidence : low , medium , or high ; sample size, sampling method, and time window; rows checked and observed violations; source/profile fingerprint and explicit assumptions. Confidence describes how strongly the conclusion is supported by the available evidence. It is not a claim that the rule is universally true. For example, observing invoice.total == sum(lines.amount) in 200 rows with no violations supports a medium-confidence hypothesis; it does not prove the domain rule. AI may rank or explain hypotheses, but it cannot increase their confidence, change their review status, or authorize generation. Missing evidence remains unknown and must either be reviewed as an explicit assumption or remain outside the executable contract. Preservation Matrix ¶ Property Preserved contract Not preserved Evidence Foreign-key graph Reviewed parent/child edges, supported cardinality, null policy, and referential integrity Source key values, row membership, or source ordering DatasetSpec relationships and relationship validation Distribution shape Configured safe ranges, ratios, bounded categories, and order of magnitude Exact histograms, rare categories, source totals, or a statistical privacy guarantee Effective field distributions and validation report Temporal dependencies Reviewed ordering rules, bounded ranges, and supported lifecycle constraints Original timestamps, event sequences, or per-source-row timing Executable temporal rules and business-validation report Business invariants Supported formulas, conditions, partitions, coverage, foreign keys, and aggregate mappings Free-form prose rules or unvalidated model conclusions Effective rule fingerprint and deterministic validation results Approval Boundary ¶ Only reviewed DatasetSpec relationships and structured business rules affect generation. Deterministic mining and AI advisors may propose candidates, but a proposal has no generation authority. Low-confidence, contradictory, stale, or unsupported candidates remain review warnings or are rejected. Scaling And Privacy ¶ Synthetic row counts and measures may scale while retaining approved relative shape and order of magnitude. Scaling must use synthetic values and explicit rules; it must not copy source totals or preserve sensitive outliers. Exact-row reuse checks are a safety backstop, not proof of anonymity. Numeric distributions accept a bounded scale_factor from 0.1 through 10.0 . Sensitive numeric distributions require an explicit non-identity factor; generation scales the approved bounds before drawing values and records the effective distribution in dataset_spec.yaml . Publication Rule ¶ A dataset may claim an invariant only when deterministic validation executes that invariant successfully. Failed or unsupported checks must block valid publication or appear as explicit controlled-invalid evidence. The manifest, effective spec, and validation reports form the review record. Validation utility evidence ¶ validation_report.json and direct validate_dataset results include additive utility evidence bound to the canonical spec_sha256 used by generation manifests. Older saved reports without this field remain readable. active_relationships and active_temporal_constraints exclude rejected declarations. Their check status is executed , not_declared , or not_run . Disabled sections and sections skipped by fail-fast are not executed. Relationship sections retain generated parent distinct-key counts, checked, resolved and null references. A measured resolution ratio of zero differs from null when there are no non-null references to check. These counts describe generated key domains, not source domains. temporal_metrics records entity, start/end field, checked row count and failed row count for each active native temporal constraint. Empty data has zero observations; business-rule evidence stays in business_validation . unmodeled_relationship_count , source_orphan_ratio and source_fanout remain null ; source_temporal_fidelity is unmeasured . Source data is not inspected by this validator. A valid report proves only the enabled declared checks, never complete relationship discovery or measured source fidelity. Evidence contains metadata and counts, not key values or temporal endpoints. Collection shares the existing generation work and deadline budget and does not add a second scan of generated rows or change seeded generation. Reviewed relational extensions ¶ Existing mixed/negative business rules can create synthetic missing-parent references. They do not provide an exact orphan-count selector, configurable fan-out allocation or measured source fan-out fidelity. Reviewed DatasetSpec explicit scenarios now provide exact synthetic orphan counts and generated-parent allocations in candidate 1.7.0rc1 source. They do not infer source histograms or reproduce source row mappings. Their executable acceptance is recorded in the controlled relational scenario change . Formulas support optional reviewed typed predicates in assign/check mode. False predicates skip evaluation and are reported separately from successful checks. See conditional formulas and the source-free EAV example. Scenario weights remain probabilistic assignments, not predicates. EAV source rows are not automatically pivoted or retained; explicit target modeling and independently generated key domains remain necessary. Explicit relational scenarios (1.7.0rc1) ¶ A reviewed DatasetSpec may include relational_scenarios . Each declaration names parent_entity , parent_field , child_entity , child_field , an exact orphan_count (default 0), and optional fanout_counts . Counts describe independently authored synthetic behavior, never observed source histograms or row mappings. See the runnable synthetic example . { "parent_entity": "parents", "parent_field": "key", "child_entity": "children", "child_field": "parent_key", "orphan_count": 2, "fanout_counts": [3, 1, 0] } With three generated parent rows and six eligible children, this assigns three children to parent ordinal 0, one to ordinal 1, none to ordinal 2, and two unique synthetic keys with no parent. Ordinals address generated row positions, never source IDs. Children with generated null keys keep their nulls and do not enter the quota. Fan-out counts plus orphans must equal the actual non-null child count; a probabilistic null ratio may therefore make a requested allocation impossible. Positive orphan counts require mixed or negative mode and invalid_ratio: 0 . Explicit scenarios use a valid synthetic field baseline, so unrelated fields do not receive random negative injection. An omitted declaration preserves existing seeded output and mode behavior. A separate deterministic RNG selects the child positions; replay needs the same ordered effective spec, seed and algorithm. Only matching integer or string keys on one unambiguous active edge are accepted. One-to-one and primary-key child targets require unique assigned keys. Fan-out requires distinct non-null generated parent keys for every positive ordinal. Conflicting key writers, negative business-rule injection, incompatible foreign-key business checks and global invalid ratios reject. Scenarios never resize tables: count overrides and load expansion are resolved first, then the authored quotas must still match. Requests are limited to 1,000 scenarios, one million parent ordinals per declaration, and existing row, cell, byte, work and deadline limits. Generation checks the complete generated key snapshot before committing changes; failed or stale allocation publishes no partial bundle. Native constraints, compatible business rules, schema and privacy remain mandatory. Writers reconcile the actual final rows again; disabling optional validation settings cannot bypass these checks for a spec with explicit scenarios. The validation report adds relational_scenarios with effective spec_sha256 , resolved sizes_sha256 , aggregate expectations_met , and count-only observations: requested/observed orphans, requested/observed fan-out, eligible and null children. Eligible minus observed orphans gives resolved references. Ambiguous repeated parent keys without an explicit fan-out return null observed fan-out. Expected missing references still set ordinary validity and manifest validation_valid to false; matching the scenario does not certify a valid dataset or source fidelity. CLI generation consequently returns the existing invalid-result exit status. The report and spec bind identity; they are not dataset approvals. CSV, JSON and Parquet can hold these explicitly controlled invalid datasets. PostgreSQL SQL export retains its valid-dataset requirement and rejects missing references before publishing DDL with foreign-key constraints. Valid fan-out allocations remain eligible for SQL export. No package release is implied by these 1.7.0rc1 source changes. Rejected relationship hypotheses do not select scenario cardinality; allocation uses the reviewed active relationship even when endpoint names match.

docs.text: Safety Model ¶ English · Русский The central invariant is: Generated output must contain newly generated values, not copied source rows. Source data may be read to derive bounded metadata. It is not used as a pool of rows to shuffle, duplicate, or export. Trust Boundaries ¶ Selective transformation is a separate mixed-origin surface in stable 1.6.0 . Its execution and approval contract requires local interactive approval of exact input/review bytes before any explicitly non-sensitive field can be preserved. Agent execution can only consume an existing matching receipt; it cannot issue or broaden approval. Sensitivity conflicts, unknown fields and default DECIMAL preservation remain blocked. Receipt integrity does not prove personhood or anonymity. Existing generation, profiling and default responses retain their source-free contracts. Private implementation review does not activate public registration. Treat all of these as untrusted: CSV, JSON, YAML, and Parquet files; paths supplied to CLI or MCP tools; profile payloads supplied by another process; business-rule files and inline rule payloads; Trino identifiers, metadata, query results, and environment variables; PostgreSQL and Trino JDBC-style endpoint strings; local PostgreSQL and Trino SQL query-source files; output directories that may contain symlinks or existing files. Defenses ¶ Sensitive data ¶ Likely PII and secrets are detected from both field names and values. Sensitive columns suppress raw top values and expose masked patterns or aggregate metadata instead. Sensitive examples use an opaque placeholder rather than intentionally preserving source values. Non-sensitive category profiles replace source values with ranked synthetic labels by default. An explicit field-scoped local allowlist may preserve only a reviewed bounded non-sensitive business enum or constant after content, cardinality, and value-length checks. Rare free text, PII, secrets, identifiers, and quasi-identifiers are never eligible. Approved exact values may appear only in local profiles, reviewed specs, deterministic generated rows, and local SQL export. External providers receive field-scoped labels, and default MCP responses, logs, and public errors remain source-literal free. Source-row reuse ¶ Generation uses a reviewed specification and a local seeded random generator. Runtime checks reject exact source-row reuse in supported CSV workflows. The comparison covers complete rows only and runs only when the source CSV is available to that workflow. It does not detect every partial-value, quasi-identifier, or statistical similarity between source and output. Filesystem ¶ Input and output paths must be distinct. New bundles are assembled in a temporary sibling directory and published only after size and validation checks. Workspace-bound MCP paths reject traversal and symlink escapes. Trino ¶ Trino access is read-only, allowlisted, bounded by client row limits and server-side time and scan budgets. Unsafe query shapes and likely sensitive projections are rejected before execution. The default aggregate-only tools return only source-literal-free metadata and aggregates. The explicit opt-in row-returning tool run_safe_select recursively masks every returned string in bounded scalar or composite values and any non-string field or value recognized as sensitive. Other non-string source values may remain, so those rows are not source-free or anonymous. PostgreSQL ¶ Direct PostgreSQL profiling uses the optional driver through a forced read-only session. Schema, table, and column allowlists are mandatory, and one shared statement/result/deadline budget bounds metadata and aggregate queries. Normal table profiling accepts no caller SQL and reads no source rows. profile-query is a separate local-file surface for one strictly parsed, single-table, fully allowlisted SELECT . Adapter-owned no-row schema and aggregate queries profile its virtual relation without fetching result rows. The profile stores a SHA-256 fingerprint and policy version, never query text, query literals, backend messages, endpoints, or source rows. Qualified local category selectors may retain only values that pass the selective local policy above. PostgreSQL schema.table.* and Trino catalog.schema.table.* column selectors are authorization syntax, not SQL. They are expanded from bounded metadata for one exact allowed table into a deterministic explicit-column snapshot before aggregates run. They do not authorize source rows, local exact values, category literals, caller projection stars, providers, default MCP literals, logs, or errors. PostgreSQL and Trino may accept credential-free JDBC-style endpoint syntax. Parsing happens before client construction and rejects userinfo, secrets, session-changing or unknown properties, malformed escapes, ambiguous paths, and conflicting component configuration. The complete URL is discarded after normalization and is never written to profiles, manifests, MCP responses, provider payloads, logs, or public errors. Resource limits ¶ The project limits input bytes, rows, columns, cells, YAML complexity, Parquet expansion, generated rows, output bytes, available disk reserve, rule work, query work, and wall-clock generation time. What The Project Guarantees ¶ For supported synthetic-generation workflows and accepted inputs, the project is designed to: avoid copying complete source rows; avoid writing raw detected PII into safe profiles; regenerate identifiers and sensitive semantic values; produce logically deterministic output for the same spec, rules, seed, locale, runtime, dependencies, serializer, and generator version; validate schema, relationships, constraints, and business rules; record provenance and safety flags in a generation manifest. The manifest records those effective inputs plus SHA-256 evidence for generated artifacts. Byte-for-byte identity is expected only when the complete recorded environment is unchanged. It is not guaranteed across Python, dependency, serializer, operating-system, or package versions, even when logical values and validation results remain equivalent. What It Does Not Guarantee ¶ The project cannot decide whether every ambiguous business field is sensitive. It also cannot prove that an inferred distribution is legally or statistically safe for every use case. The project does not currently implement differential privacy, k-anonymity, l-diversity, or a privacy budget, and makes no statistical privacy guarantee. Treat generated data as requiring a domain-specific privacy review before distribution. Human review is still required for: domain-specific identifiers and rare free text; inferred relationships and constraints; privacy requirements outside the built-in detectors; organization-specific retention and access controls; downstream systems that may log or redistribute generated data. Do not send production data, raw PII, credentials, or tokens to an LLM while reviewing profiles or specifications. Acceptance Checklist ¶ Before publishing a generated dataset: This checklist applies to synthetic generation, not the gated mixed-origin transformation workflow. A transformed bundle must not be relabelled synthetic merely because validation passed: its action provenance and any matching local preservation receipt remain separate requirements. manifest says synthetic: true ; manifest says source_rows_copied: false ; deterministic validation passed; business validation passed when rules were used; seed, row counts, format, and fingerprints are correct; profile and generated samples contain no unexpected sensitive values; the output is stored outside the source path. See Review The Output for the practical review sequence. Configured SQL Transformation Sessions ¶ The separately selected configured query workflow captures one allowlisted read-only result using administrator configuration, then reviews and validates frozen local bytes without reconnecting. It does not expand ordinary profiling or source-free generation authority. MCP returns only metadata and consumes an existing exact local controlling-TTY receipt when preservation requires one; it cannot issue approval. Session handles expire without recapture, owned raw inputs/receipts are removed, and only validated selected output is retained. Cleanup failure refuses further work. Registration is not data access permission or final exact-SHA security/release clearance.

docs.text: Generation uses a reviewed specification and a local seeded random generator. Runtime checks reject exact source-row reuse in supported CSV workflows. The comparison covers complete rows only and runs only when the source CSV is available to that workflow. It does not detect every partial-value, quasi-identifier, or statistical similarity between source and output.
docs.title: Source-row reuse

docs.text: Input and output paths must be distinct. New bundles are assembled in a temporary sibling directory and published only after size and validation checks. Workspace-bound MCP paths reject traversal and symlink escapes.
docs.title: Filesystem

docs.text: Trino access is read-only, allowlisted, bounded by client row limits and server-side time and scan budgets. Unsafe query shapes and likely sensitive projections are rejected before execution. The default aggregate-only tools return only source-literal-free metadata and aggregates. The explicit opt-in row-returning tool run_safe_select recursively masks every returned string in bounded scalar or composite values and any non-string field or value recognized as sensitive. Other non-string source values may remain, so those rows are not source-free or anonymous.
docs.title: Trino

docs.text: Direct PostgreSQL profiling uses the optional driver through a forced read-only session. Schema, table, and column allowlists are mandatory, and one shared statement/result/deadline budget bounds metadata and aggregate queries. Normal table profiling accepts no caller SQL and reads no source rows. profile-query is a separate local-file surface for one strictly parsed, single-table, fully allowlisted SELECT . Adapter-owned no-row schema and aggregate queries profile its virtual relation without fetching result rows. The profile stores a SHA-256 fingerprint and policy version, never query text, query literals, backend messages, endpoints, or source rows. Qualified local category selectors may retain only values that pass the selective local policy above. PostgreSQL schema.table.* and Trino catalog.schema.table.* column selectors are authorization syntax, not SQL. They are expanded from bounded metadata for one exact allowed table into a deterministic explicit-column snapshot before aggregates run. They do not authorize source rows, local exact values, category literals, caller projection stars, providers, default MCP literals, logs, or errors. PostgreSQL and Trino may accept credential-free JDBC-style endpoint syntax. Parsing happens before client construction and rejects userinfo, secrets, session-changing or unknown properties, malformed escapes, ambiguous paths, and conflicting component configuration. The complete URL is discarded after normalization and is never written to profiles, manifests, MCP responses, provider payloads, logs, or public errors.
docs.title: PostgreSQL

docs.text: The project limits input bytes, rows, columns, cells, YAML complexity, Parquet expansion, generated rows, output bytes, available disk reserve, rule work, query work, and wall-clock generation time.
docs.title: Resource limits

docs.text: For supported synthetic-generation workflows and accepted inputs, the project is designed to: avoid copying complete source rows; avoid writing raw detected PII into safe profiles; regenerate identifiers and sensitive semantic values; produce logically deterministic output for the same spec, rules, seed, locale, runtime, dependencies, serializer, and generator version; validate schema, relationships, constraints, and business rules; record provenance and safety flags in a generation manifest. The manifest records those effective inputs plus SHA-256 evidence for generated artifacts. Byte-for-byte identity is expected only when the complete recorded environment is unchanged. It is not guaranteed across Python, dependency, serializer, operating-system, or package versions, even when logical values and validation results remain equivalent.
docs.title: What The Project Guarantees

docs.text: The project cannot decide whether every ambiguous business field is sensitive. It also cannot prove that an inferred distribution is legally or statistically safe for every use case. The project does not currently implement differential privacy, k-anonymity, l-diversity, or a privacy budget, and makes no statistical privacy guarantee. Treat generated data as requiring a domain-specific privacy review before distribution. Human review is still required for: domain-specific identifiers and rare free text; inferred relationships and constraints; privacy requirements outside the built-in detectors; organization-specific retention and access controls; downstream systems that may log or redistribute generated data. Do not send production data, raw PII, credentials, or tokens to an LLM while reviewing profiles or specifications.
docs.title: What It Does Not Guarantee

docs.text: Before publishing a generated dataset: This checklist applies to synthetic generation, not the gated mixed-origin transformation workflow. A transformed bundle must not be relabelled synthetic merely because validation passed: its action provenance and any matching local preservation receipt remain separate requirements. manifest says synthetic: true ; manifest says source_rows_copied: false ; deterministic validation passed; business validation passed when rules were used; seed, row counts, format, and fingerprints are correct; profile and generated samples contain no unexpected sensitive values; the output is stored outside the source path. See Review The Output for the practical review sequence.
docs.title: Acceptance Checklist

docs.text: The separately selected configured query workflow captures one allowlisted read-only result using administrator configuration, then reviews and validates frozen local bytes without reconnecting. It does not expand ordinary profiling or source-free generation authority. MCP returns only metadata and consumes an existing exact local controlling-TTY receipt when preservation requires one; it cannot issue approval. Session handles expire without recapture, owned raw inputs/receipts are removed, and only validated selected output is retained. Cleanup failure refuses further work. Registration is not data access permission or final exact-SHA security/release clearance.
docs.title: Configured SQL Transformation Sessions

docs.text: Threat Model ¶ English · Русский This model covers supported CSV, Python, CLI, MCP, Trino, advisor, generation, validation, and export workflows. The primary security objective is to prevent source rows, raw detected PII, and secrets from crossing into generated output, provider requests, logs, or unrestricted database operations. Assets And Trust Boundaries ¶ Protected assets are source datasets, credentials, connection settings, reviewed specifications, generated artifacts, manifests, and validation reports. Treat every source file, rule payload, profile, path, Trino response, MCP request, advisor response, and output destination as untrusted. The main boundaries are: local source to bounded profiler; profiler and reviewed specification to deterministic generator; application to optional AI provider; MCP client to workspace-confined tools; application to read-only Trino; staged artifacts to the published output directory. Threats And Controls ¶ Threat Control Residual risk Source rows or raw PII reach generated output Profiles suppress sensitive values; specs pass assert_spec_safe() ; supported CSV flows reject complete-row reuse. Partial values, rare combinations, and statistical similarity require human review. Secrets leak through input, configuration, logs, or provider calls Secret-like fields and values are treated as sensitive; provider requests use bounded structured evidence; rejected values are not echoed. Unknown secret formats or unsafe downstream logging can bypass heuristics. Prompt injection in source text or advisor output changes authority Source text is untrusted data, provider schemas are validated, and AI proposals require explicit human review; deterministic code alone authorizes generation and validation. A reviewer can still approve a misleading proposal. Never send raw production content to a provider. Provider receives source records or rare identifying values Advisor payloads exclude rows, replace categories with synthetic labels, and sanitize singleton values before the provider boundary. Provider retention and transport remain governed by the selected provider and operator configuration. Trino access reads sensitive rows or mutates data Public operations are allowlisted, read-only, and bounded; unsafe SQL is rejected before execution; credentials stay outside returned payloads. Database permissions must independently enforce least privilege and read-only access. MCP paths escape the configured workspace or overwrite trusted files Path traversal and symlink escapes are rejected; source and output paths must differ; publication is staged and atomic. Operators must secure the workspace and downstream artifact storage. Generated artifacts are mistaken for privacy-certified data Manifests record synthetic and validation evidence; documentation separates structural validation from privacy assurance. The project provides no differential privacy, anonymity, or universal re-identification guarantee. Oversized inputs, queries, rules, or output exhaust resources Byte, row, cell, nesting, query, rule, disk, output, and wall-clock budgets fail closed. Limits reduce impact but do not replace process, container, or infrastructure quotas. Modified packages or artifacts enter the release path Release gates produce checksums, SBOMs, attestations, and exact-commit evidence. Users must verify published evidence and protect their installation environment. Assumptions And Non-Goals ¶ Operators keep credentials outside datasets and logs, grant Trino least privilege, review inferred rules, and protect generated artifacts. The project does not defend a compromised host, malicious Python code running in the same process, a compromised dependency, or redistribution by an authorized user. It does not certify legal compliance or statistical privacy. Report suspected boundary failures through the private process in the Security Policy . Use synthetic reproductions only.

docs.text: Parallel Cloudflare Pages Publication ¶ The maintainer selected Cloudflare Pages on 2026-11-01 after the RTD Community experiment. The active change is migrate-documentation-to-cloudflare-pages . This is preparation for a parallel deployment, not a completed hosting switch. GitHub Pages remains accepted. No paid plan, custom domain, DNS change, package release or tag rewrite is required by this implementation. Build And Trust Boundary ¶ Keep the existing strict GitHub Documentation workflow, frozen Python/docs packages, Chromium PDF exporter, release verification, mike editions and retained rendered artifacts. Cloudflare receives prebuilt assets through Direct Upload; it does not need to run the Python build or receive private source data. Cloudflare documentation parallel acceptance runs manually from main only. Its source-run gate requires a completed successful main-push run of .github/workflows/docs.yml in this repository, binds the exact source SHA and then downloads only that run's documentation-site artifact. PR, fork, failed, running and unrelated workflow sources are rejected before publication. The uploader executes only trusted main deployment code in an empty working directory. Site artifacts are data: symlinks, Worker/Functions entrypoints and host/tool configuration are rejected. All local edition/entry/export hashes are checked before upload. Credential access belongs only to the pinned Cloudflare action steps; no PR source is checked out or run with that credential. Initial uploads always use migration-RUN_ID , never the production branch. The payload adds only _headers : noindex for parallel publication and attachment headers for standalone HTML, covering both .html and Cloudflare's extensionless paths at root and in version directories. Page/export bytes and recorded hashes are preserved. The Free-plan preflight uses 20,000 files and 25 MiB per asset. A retained real site passed with 1,212 files, 91,676,529 bytes and five editions; this is a local payload result, not evidence of a Cloudflare upload. Owner Setup ¶ Use an existing Cloudflare account. Create a Pages Direct Upload project with production branch main , or choose create_project=true on the first workflow run to create it through the reviewed uploader. Do not select Git integration for this project. A project name and actual pages.dev addresses are not yet assumed available. Create the GitHub environment cloudflare-pages-preview , restricted to main. Configure these values in that environment: Name Kind Value CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID Variable The selected account's 32-character ID CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT Variable The chosen Direct Upload project name CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN Secret Scoped Cloudflare API token described below The official Direct Upload integration requires Account → Cloudflare Pages → Edit , limited to the intended account. This is an account-wide Pages permission; it must not be described as limited to one project. Use a dedicated token and revoke it when no longer needed. The token does not need DNS, zone, Worker/KV/R2 or repository administration permissions. The owner must review the actual permission screen before creating it. Never paste the token into chat, a file, workflow input, repository variable, command history or screenshot. Transfer it directly from Cloudflare to the named GitHub environment secret; the agent does not need to read its value. First Parallel Deployment ¶ Select a successful main Documentation run with a retained, unexpired documentation-site artifact. Run 41284167968 is an observed example at 2ea24cfebc74356c53c0117ca094ee9d60961cb9 , not a permanent default source. Run Cloudflare documentation parallel acceptance from main with that numeric source_run_id . Select create_project only for the first project creation. Inspect the returned immutable deployment URL. The verifier retains the mike stable alias/destination gate, compares each edition's public identity, chapter/manifest inventory, exact entry bytes and all four exports against that same downloaded build, and requires HTML attachment headers. A failed check leaves the accepted GitHub Pages site and canonical links unchanged. Uploading a parallel branch is not production promotion. The first workflow does not implement automatic PR publishing, managed production promotion, canonical replacement or hosted rollback. Those remain required tasks in the active OpenSpec. Existing RTD/GitHub Pages resources are retained until equivalent Cloudflare functionality and recovery are verified. docs.text: Publishing Documentation ¶ Tools And Local Preview ¶ Hosting remains GitHub Pages . MkDocs renders pages, mike owns version storage, aliases and the version selector, and mkdocs-print-site-plugin assembles the printable handbook. HTMLArk embeds its assets; Chrome prints PDF. Read the Docs integration is being prepared in parallel; no host switch or verified Read the Docs project URL has been recorded. The theme name alone does not connect a service. See parallel hosting preparation . uv sync --frozen --only-group docs --no-install-project uv run --no-sync mkdocs build --strict uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.build_documentation --output site --verify-release --state-bundle site.bundle python3 -m http.server --directory site 8000 The complete build needs Chrome/Chromium. Pass --browser PATH if necessary. It uses a temporary browser profile and blocks DNS; HTML embedding can read only resources inside the rendered site. Documentation export never reads datasets, receipts, credentials or user browser profiles. A plain mkdocs serve includes the print page but does not generate download files. The small project adapter verifies release evidence, attaches provenance, keeps legacy root URLs, scopes search and packages downloads. It delegates rendering, version storage, aliases and selector behavior to the installed tools. The locked documentation group is separate from runtime package dependencies. Versions And Compatibility ¶ Location Meaning Site root Maintained guide for the verified stable package; existing URLs work versions/stable/ mike's copy alias to the selected stable guide, with selector versions/X.Y.Z/ Guide for that exact package version, with its own search index versions/X.Y.ZrcN/ Exact release-candidate guide, explicitly not stable versions/next/ Current development guide or copy alias of the latest RC documentation.json Package version/source, documentation revision and status downloads/ PDF, standalone HTML, Markdown source ZIP, selected-version site ZIP A package-version guide may receive reviewed documentation corrections while it is current. Its metadata records the documentation commit separately from the package release commit. It is not an untouched snapshot of the release-era prose , and it does not inherit the package's exact-SHA review. Once another package becomes current, older rendered guides remain unchanged unless an explicitly reviewed correction is published for them. Never relabel today's prose as guidance for an unsupported historical package. mike stores generated versions and aliases in the gh-pages branch. That branch is publication state, not a source branch. The root tree is a compatibility copy of maintained stable guidance; it links to the native version selector. All other versions have independent search indexes. Historical/maintainer pages remain available through the history index but are excluded from default search. Local builds use refs/remotes/origin/gh-pages when available. Fetch it first to retain existing versions, or pass --state-ref REF to a local branch containing previous native state. First publication bootstraps only the current verified stable package; it does not manufacture earlier snapshots. A development or RC build requires already-published stable state and preserves the complete stable root. RC builds retain their exact version directory and move only the next copy alias; later candidates preserve earlier RC directories. RC identity binds to its tag commit once available and otherwise to the candidate source. The label does not claim successful package publication or public acceptance. Publication And Release Gates ¶ Finish the existing exact-source package release gates and public verification. Add its stable version, exact release commit and successful public-verification run ID to docs/releases.json ; retain prior catalog entries. Advance stable only for the publicly verified stable package. RCs stay out of this pointer. Review guides and fictional installed-package examples against that package. Run focused documentation checks and inspect the complete export. Merge the reviewed source change. The main-only Pages workflow verifies the catalog, builds all formats and publishes the complete Pages artifact. Public verification compares exact metadata, the native stable alias/destination, entry-page hash and all four download hashes. Only after that succeeds does a separate write-scoped job retain the native mike Git bundle in gh-pages , without force-pushing. PR builds have read-only repository permissions and never push state. Complete main publications are serialized. Build/export failure leaves the deployed site untouched. A failure after Pages deployment requires restoring a retained prior successful Pages artifact; public verification is not an atomic deployment and there is no automatic rollback. If retaining mike state fails after successful verification, restore the matching documentation-mike-state workflow artifact before another publication, so version history is not lost. Artifacts are retained for 90 days; gh-pages retains published version history. Builds use a disposable Git repository and cannot change a developer's branches. Local site replacement is staged and restores the prior output on handled errors or interruptions. If another writer prevents restoration, recover the preserved sibling .apa-docs-backup-* directory manually. Checks ¶ uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_documentation.py tests/test_documentation_build.py uv run --no-sync mkdocs build --strict Tests require both the documentation group and development test dependencies. The PDF and standalone HTML contain the current navigation's user chapters, excluding history, roadmap and documentation administration. The Markdown ZIP preserves the full documentation source tree so reference links remain reusable; historical pages keep their original provenance. The site ZIP contains one selected version, without recursively including other versions or its own ZIP. Russian Edition ¶ docs/ru/ mirrors current user-guide paths. Keep translated command blocks and review gates synchronized with their English counterpart; untranslated specialist API tutorials and historical records must be labelled English rather than presented as translated content. docs/ru/quality-report.md records example and build evidence, including checks that were not run. The existing theme switches to the Russian navigation for ru/ pages. Its English / Русский links resolve within the current mike version; a missing counterpart falls back to the other language's home with an explicit label. Markdown language links also work in the repository. Built-in search indexes both English and Russian, while the history classification normalizes ru/ . No new localization plugin or runtime dependency is required. The combined PDF/HTML handbook is bilingual. Print-site and the export chapter manifest exclude history, roadmap, downloads and versions for both languages. Markdown and offline-site ZIPs include both editions. Do not make language switches point to the unversioned production root: that would silently change the package version when reading an older guide. Hosting Decision And Retained RTD Evaluation ¶ On 2026-11-01 the maintainer selected Cloudflare Pages for the migration. Continue with parallel Cloudflare publication and migrate-documentation-to-cloudflare-pages . The RTD material below retains actual experiment evidence; it is not the selected future hosting plan. Parallel Read the Docs Preparation ¶ The active OpenSpec is migrate-documentation-to-readthedocs . GitHub Pages remains the accepted publication while service access and public acceptance are incomplete. The original connected-service failure has no confirmed cause. The maintainer subsequently imported the public project; native normal and PR builds now succeed. The evidence and remaining serving constraints are recorded below. Reuse And Host Responsibilities ¶ Existing component Parallel build decision mkdocs.yml , docs/ , bilingual theme/search Keep; use the host-provided edition canonical URL scripts/documentation_hooks.py Reuse identity, scoped search, chapter inventory and all four exporters docs/releases.json Keep accepted stable package identities; a host alias cannot replace release evidence scripts/build_documentation.py Retain Pages/mike publication, compatibility root, snapshots and atomic local output scripts/build_readthedocs.py Render one isolated edition; no mike tree, deployment credentials, default changes or Pages writes .github/workflows/docs.yml Retain licenses, strict builds, focused contracts, release verification, Pages deployment and public checks scripts/verify_documentation.py Retain all existing public Pages checks; its mike-specific mapping is not an RTD acceptance check Pages build artifacts and gh-pages Retain recovery bundle, rendered output and existing 90-day retention; no cleanup during parallel testing Normal RTD builds use the same PDF, standalone HTML, Markdown ZIP and offline site ZIP exporters. documentation.json preserves package version, package source and documentation revision separately. A development build can describe a released candidate while having a newer documentation revision. A tagged build must match a clean checkout and its package tag. A stable tag is labelled as awaiting public acceptance; its build alone does not prove a public release or agreement with the accepted catalog. This builder does not establish an accepted stable/default mapping. Development package versions such as 1.7.0.dev1 remain labelled development, including when built from a tag; they cannot acquire stable status. PR builds ( READTHEDOCS_VERSION_TYPE=external ) have a visible preview label, noindex , and bilingual download pages explaining that downloads are omitted. They do not install the export browser. Normal builds require all four exports; a failed strict build/export leaves the previous local output intact. Tooling And Local Reproduction ¶ .readthedocs.yaml selects Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12 and uv 0.11.23. Host jobs invoke python -m uv through the interpreter used to install it, so they do not depend on the installed console script being on PATH . Installation uses the frozen docs-only dependency group without installing the application. Playwright is a docs-only browser distributor; its locked version selects Chromium for the existing PDF exporter. It does not automate accounts or use a user's browser profile. License checking runs before rendering. uv sync --frozen --only-group docs --no-install-project --python 3.12 uv run --no-sync python scripts/check_dependency_licenses.py uv run --no-sync playwright install --no-shell chromium READTHEDOCS_VERSION_TYPE=branch \ READTHEDOCS_GIT_IDENTIFIER=main \ READTHEDOCS_CANONICAL_URL=https://example.invalid/en/latest/ \ uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.build_readthedocs --output /tmp/apa-rtd/html Package tags are fetched explicitly after checkout so shallow service clones do not silently lose released package provenance. The example URL is fictional, not a deployed project. On the host, the builder uses READTHEDOCS_CANONICAL_URL , verifies READTHEDOCS_GIT_COMMIT_HASH against the checkout, and writes HTML plus downloads under READTHEDOCS_OUTPUT/html . Ubuntu browser libraries and fonts are declared through RTD's supported build.apt_packages , based on the locked Playwright Chromium dependency list; installation does not require an ad hoc privileged shell command. Native execution was confirmed by build 35554945; a successful build still does not prove public byte integrity or accepted version/default mappings. Account Setup And Acceptance Still Required ¶ The Community service documents a 15-minute build limit, 7 GB memory and two concurrent builds. Confirm the actual account plan and configured limits. The public project is imported and produces PR checks. Owner-only work still includes reviewing the installed GitHub App repository selection/permissions and private-variable isolation, and configuring version activation/defaults. Build success does not prove these settings. Do not store private environment variables or publishing credentials in preview builds. A paid plan, custom domain or broader repository access is not assumed. The documented GitHub App permissions are: read account email, repository contents and metadata; write commit statuses, pull requests and checks; read organization membership where applicable. Select only wa-pis/agent-paranoid-android when granting repository access. The actual permission screen must be reviewed before installation; these documented permissions are not evidence of an installed or authorized app. See the service integration reference . Do not let automatic stable tag selection act as release acceptance. Before switching any canonical/default URL, the remaining work must prove accepted stable/candidate/development mappings, faithful historical documentation refs or retained snapshots, public release evidence, bilingual navigation/search, old links and anchors, all four downloaded hashes and rollback. Immutable old tags lacking host configuration stay intact. Upstream source preflight at RTD commit f343b74 shows a plan-dependent constraint: the settings form disables the global Addons switch outside Business , and the serving middleware requests injection when the global flag is enabled . Turning off an individual flyout/search option must not be assumed to remove HTML injection. This is source-based preflight evidence, not an observation of our project's deployed settings. Business has not been selected or purchased. Read the Docs can inject add-ons into served HTML. The current Pages verifier checks the exact entry-page bytes as well as download bytes: host injection must be resolved and verified against actual served output, not accommodated by silently dropping the entry-page integrity check. No host acceptance or retirement of Pages is implied by a successful local build. Verify the standalone handbook.html download as well as the entry page on the actual service: its original bytes, manifest digest and ability to work offline must survive hosting. Do not silently exempt either file from verification, assume a paid setting exists in Community, or label an untested workaround as accepted. References: configuration , environment , build limits , PR previews , browser versions . Native Service Evidence — 2026-11-01 ¶ The public project is agent-paranoid-android . Normal build 35554945 succeeded at documentation revision 0991058d08067284b8346a05c62944bd71131a57 . Its latest edition correctly identifies package 1.7.0rc1 , package source 64b7c8c3bbb0174fd7e159c4dfb42312045a1716 , and Development / not stable . PR build 35554849 also succeeded for PR #671 at 5e2115b0386e9d039d248a112003bd48722d1b91 . These are native service results, not only GitHub build simulations. docs.text: Hosting remains GitHub Pages . MkDocs renders pages, mike owns version storage, aliases and the version selector, and mkdocs-print-site-plugin assembles the printable handbook. HTMLArk embeds its assets; Chrome prints PDF. Read the Docs integration is being prepared in parallel; no host switch or verified Read the Docs project URL has been recorded. The theme name alone does not connect a service. See parallel hosting preparation . uv sync --frozen --only-group docs --no-install-project uv run --no-sync mkdocs build --strict uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.build_documentation --output site --verify-release --state-bundle site.bundle python3 -m http.server --directory site 8000 The complete build needs Chrome/Chromium. Pass --browser PATH if necessary. It uses a temporary browser profile and blocks DNS; HTML embedding can read only resources inside the rendered site. Documentation export never reads datasets, receipts, credentials or user browser profiles. A plain mkdocs serve includes the print page but does not generate download files. The small project adapter verifies release evidence, attaches provenance, keeps legacy root URLs, scopes search and packages downloads. It delegates rendering, version storage, aliases and selector behavior to the installed tools. The locked documentation group is separate from runtime package dependencies.

docs.text: Location Meaning Site root Maintained guide for the verified stable package; existing URLs work versions/stable/ mike's copy alias to the selected stable guide, with selector versions/X.Y.Z/ Guide for that exact package version, with its own search index versions/X.Y.ZrcN/ Exact release-candidate guide, explicitly not stable versions/next/ Current development guide or copy alias of the latest RC documentation.json Package version/source, documentation revision and status downloads/ PDF, standalone HTML, Markdown source ZIP, selected-version site ZIP A package-version guide may receive reviewed documentation corrections while it is current. Its metadata records the documentation commit separately from the package release commit. It is not an untouched snapshot of the release-era prose , and it does not inherit the package's exact-SHA review. Once another package becomes current, older rendered guides remain unchanged unless an explicitly reviewed correction is published for them. Never relabel today's prose as guidance for an unsupported historical package. mike stores generated versions and aliases in the gh-pages branch. That branch is publication state, not a source branch. The root tree is a compatibility copy of maintained stable guidance; it links to the native version selector. All other versions have independent search indexes. Historical/maintainer pages remain available through the history index but are excluded from default search. Local builds use refs/remotes/origin/gh-pages when available. Fetch it first to retain existing versions, or pass --state-ref REF to a local branch containing previous native state. First publication bootstraps only the current verified stable package; it does not manufacture earlier snapshots. A development or RC build requires already-published stable state and preserves the complete stable root. RC builds retain their exact version directory and move only the next copy alias; later candidates preserve earlier RC directories. RC identity binds to its tag commit once available and otherwise to the candidate source. The label does not claim successful package publication or public acceptance.

docs.text: Finish the existing exact-source package release gates and public verification. Public verification compares exact metadata, the native stable alias/destination, entry-page hash and all four download hashes. Only after that succeeds does a separate write-scoped job retain the native mike Git bundle in gh-pages , without force-pushing. PR builds have read-only repository permissions and never push state. Complete main publications are serialized. Build/export failure leaves the deployed site untouched. A failure after Pages deployment requires restoring a retained prior successful Pages artifact; public verification is not an atomic deployment and there is no automatic rollback. Artifacts are retained for 90 days; gh-pages retains published version history. Builds use a disposable Git repository and cannot change a developer's branches. Local site replacement is staged and restores the prior output on handled errors or interruptions. docs.text: .readthedocs.yaml selects Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12 and uv 0.11.23. Do not silently exempt either file from verification, assume a paid setting exists in Community, or label an untested workaround as accepted. docs.text: First CSV Dataset ¶ English · Русский This tutorial profiles one CSV file, infers a generation specification, generates new values, and validates the result. Prerequisites ¶ complete Installation ; run commands from a clone of this repository so the synthetic fixture below is available; choose a new output directory. The fixture contains fictional values and reserved example email domains. For the same workflow as an executable script with its own synthetic fixture, run examples/csv_quickstart/run.sh . Generate 25 Rows ¶ test-data-agent generate-from-csv tests/fixtures/customers.csv \ --count 25 \ --seed 12345 \ --format csv \ --output out/customers.csv Expected summary: Generated synthetic dataset: out | rows: customers=25 | seed: 12345 | validation: passed | source rows copied: no The exact output path shown in the summary can vary by platform. Inspect The Bundle ¶ The command writes: out/ customers.csv csv_profile.json dataset_spec.json generation_manifest.json validation_report.json Check the manifest before using the data: python3 -c "import json; m=json.load(open('out/generation_manifest.json')); print(m['synthetic'], m['source_rows_copied'], m['validation_valid'], m['seed'])" Expected output: True False True 12345 Open out/customers.csv and confirm that it contains 25 generated rows plus the header. Source rows are not shuffled or copied. Reproduce The Result ¶ Generate into a different path with the same seed: test-data-agent generate-from-csv tests/fixtures/customers.csv \ --count 25 \ --seed 12345 \ --format csv \ --output out/repeated/customers.csv The two generated CSV files should match: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; assert Path('out/customers.csv').read_bytes() == Path('out/repeated/customers.csv').read_bytes(); print('deterministic: ok')" Use Your Own CSV ¶ Replace the fixture path with your file: test-data-agent generate-from-csv data/customers.csv \ --count 100 \ --seed 12345 \ --format csv \ --output out/customers.csv Treat every source CSV as potentially sensitive. Do not share its contents, profile artifacts, or command logs until you have reviewed them. The profiler suppresses raw values for fields detected as sensitive, but ambiguous domain fields still require human review. Exact values remain replaced by default. When customers.status has been reviewed as a bounded non-sensitive business enum, authorize only that field: test-data-agent generate-from-csv tests/fixtures/customers.csv \ --local-category customers.status \ --count 25 \ --seed 12345 \ --format csv \ --output out/approved-status/customers.csv The request fails closed if the field contains PII, secrets, identifiers, quasi-identifiers, free text, excessive cardinality, or long values. The option does not authorize any other field or any external-provider destination. Review ambiguous identifiers and financial columns before accepting inferred keys or distributions. For exact category limits, distinct-count evidence and identifier behavior, see CSV Profiling Details . Next, read Review The Output .

docs.text: Product Validation Pilot ¶ English · Русский Use this guide when you want to evaluate the product with a real development or analytics task. It is intentionally shorter than a production rollout: the goal is to learn whether the generated dataset is useful and whether the review flow is understandable. The User Problem ¶ The product is useful when a team has enough structure and examples to describe a source system, but cannot give developers the source rows themselves. Potential evidence inputs include: SQL DDL with primary keys, foreign keys, and checks; Django, SQLAlchemy, or another ORM model description; a bounded sample or safe profile with representative distributions; a short description of the business invariants that must reconcile. CSV files or folders, validated safe profiles and optional PostgreSQL and Trino integrations are available in stable 1.5.0 . Stable 1.6.0 retains these and the accepted RC5 profile-parquet route for one Parquet file with the optional parquet extra, followed by reviewed spec inference or an authored DatasetSpec ; see release status . Unknown null statistics require an authored spec; exact DECIMAL inference requires reviewed bounds. PostgreSQL uses mandatory schema/table/column allowlists and bounded aggregate profiling; see the PostgreSQL workflow and source/output matrix . SQL DDL, Django models and SQLAlchemy models are not first-class CLI inputs. The output is a fresh synthetic dataset for development, integration tests, analytics changes, forecasting, or budgeting experiments. It is not a masked copy of the source and it is not a privacy certification. Exact values are replaced by default. A reviewer may explicitly preserve a bounded non-sensitive business enum or constant for local generation and SQL export; that exception is field-scoped, fails closed on unsafe content, and never extends to source rows, external providers, or default MCP responses. AI Is Optional ¶ The core workflow does not require an AI provider, an MCP client, or an internet connection. A user can profile input, review or edit a DatasetSpec , generate data, and validate it with the CLI or Python API using deterministic code. AI is an optional accelerator for the parts that are expensive for a human to do manually: Situation Value of AI Authority DDL or ORM models already declare all relationships and rules Usually little; use the deterministic CLI path Deterministic profile and human review Foreign keys are missing or ambiguous Rank and explain bounded relationship hypotheses Human accepts or rejects; deterministic checks validate Field names and examples imply domain semantics Suggest semantic types or candidate business rules Human confirms; deterministic generation enforces Final generation and validation No special value; AI must not generate rows or approve silently Deterministic code and explicit approval Do not add AI merely because the product is called an agent. First run the workflow without it. Add an advisor only when it reduces manual discovery or helps a reviewer understand evidence that is otherwise difficult to inspect. Optional AI-Assisted Review Prompt ¶ Use the following prompt only when an AI client is being evaluated as part of the pilot. It is not required for the deterministic CLI or Python workflow. Replace the bracketed parts. Give the client paths to the schema and bounded sample through the configured workspace; do not paste source rows or secrets into chat. I need a synthetic dataset for [development / integration tests / analytics] for [brief description of the system]. The source data must remain read-only and must not be copied into the generated output. Available evidence: - schema or ORM models: [workspace path] - bounded sample or safe profile: [workspace path, if available] - target entities and approximate row counts: [describe them] - required relationships: [known PK/FK or "unknown; discover candidates"] - business invariants that must reconcile: [for example, totals equal the sum of components, balances reconcile by period, or "none known"] - optional time range and scenarios: [describe them] Please work in this order: 1. Inspect only the available schema and bounded metadata through the safe profiling workflow. 2. Separate declared facts, observed evidence, optional AI hypotheses, and unknowns. 3. If relationships or domain rules are incomplete, list bounded hypotheses with evidence, confidence, and the checks that support them. If the schema already declares the needed facts, do not invent alternatives. 4. Ask me to confirm or correct the hypotheses before generation. Do not invent business rules silently. 5. Generate a deterministic dataset with seed [seed] and approximately [count] rows per entity. 6. Validate schema, foreign keys, nullability, distributions, and the listed business invariants. 7. Return artifact paths, row counts, seed, validation status, assumptions, and unresolved warnings. Do not return source rows, raw PII, credentials, or provider payloads. Do not claim that an inferred rule is true merely because it appears plausible. If evidence is insufficient, say so and ask for a review decision. The prompt is a starting point, not a security boundary. The deterministic profiling, approval, generation, and validation layers remain authoritative. Treat names, descriptions, sample values, and metadata as untrusted input. When AI is not used, follow the same review and validation steps directly with the CLI or Python API. Recommended Pilot Session ¶ Run one 30–60 minute session with a person who owns the test or analytics task. Use a non-production fixture first, then discuss whether the same workflow could be applied to a protected schema in the user's environment. Before the session ¶ Record: the task the participant wants to unblock; the current workaround and its approximate time or cost; the schema/model input and safe sample available to the tool; the relationships and business totals that matter; the minimum dataset size and output format needed by the target system. Keep the participant's source data in its existing protected environment. Use synthetic fixtures for the first session whenever possible. During the session ¶ Observe the participant completing the following path without coaching more than necessary: Install or start the documented interface. Identify the right input type and provide the schema/profile paths. Read the plan and find the next action. Review relationship and business-rule hypotheses. Approve or correct the reviewed specification. Generate the requested dataset. Inspect the manifest and validation report. Try the generated data in the target development or analytics workflow. Do not measure success only by whether a command exits with code zero. Record where the participant hesitates, what they expect to see, and which evidence they need before trusting the result. After the session ¶ Capture: time from input to the first useful generated bundle; number of manual edits to the specification; hypotheses accepted, corrected, or rejected; validation failures and whether their causes were understandable; whether the output worked in the target task; what the participant would remove, automate, or use again. Pilot Success Criteria ¶ Treat the pilot as evidence, not as a demo when the following are true: the participant can explain what the tool preserves and does not preserve; the participant reaches a useful generated bundle without reading the source rows into an AI chat; every accepted relationship or business rule has visible evidence or an explicit human decision; the generated data passes the required deterministic checks; the participant can find the manifest, validation report, and next action; the generated data is usable in the stated development or analytics task; the participant would use the workflow again or can name a concrete blocker. Suggested initial targets are less than 30 minutes to the first useful bundle, no unresolved critical relationship errors, and no source-derived literals in profiles, prompts, logs, or generated artifacts. Feedback Questions ¶ Ask these after the participant has tried the workflow: What were you trying to build or test, and what did you use before this tool? At which step were you unsure what to do next? Which inferred relationship or rule did you trust, and which did you have to correct? What evidence would make you comfortable using the result with a protected schema? Did the generated data preserve the relationships, scale, nullability, and reconciliations your task required? What did you expect to be preserved that the tool deliberately did not preserve? What output or integration step still required manual work? If this workflow disappeared tomorrow, what would you replace it with? Would you run it again? If not, what is the first blocker to remove? Do Not Over-Interpret A Pilot ¶ One successful fixture does not prove that the product works for every domain or that the output is anonymous. Record the input type, sample size, sampling method, evidence coverage, participant task, and unresolved assumptions. A pilot can validate usability and task fit; it cannot replace domain privacy review, security review, or deterministic validation. Next read Review The Output for the artifact checks that must follow generation.
