docs.text: Configuration ¶ English · Русский Defaults are conservative. Raise limits only after reviewing expected data volume, available resources, and the trust level of the input. These settings describe stable 1.6.0 . Historical anchors remain available. Configuration and tool registration do not grant dataset permission or local preservation approval. Existing component settings and exact allowlists remain supported. All byte values are integer bytes unless stated otherwise. CLI flags override the corresponding command defaults. Environment variables configure resource, database, provider, and transport boundaries only where listed below; they do not silently activate an optional provider or overwrite an explicit CLI value. Use COMMAND --help to inspect CLI defaults and doctor --json for installed/local capability states. doctor deliberately does not read provider credentials or test remote reachability. Common Transformation Profile ¶ Stable 1.6.0 provides the common CLI/MCP workflow. Its versioned reference profile combines two or more inputs with one independently reviewed DatasetSpec for final linked validation: schema_version: "0.1" validation: validation.yaml inputs: - entity: fictional_parents source: parents.csv policy: parents-policy.yaml - entity: fictional_children source: children.csv policy: children-policy.yaml mappings: [keys.csv] mappings and generation_policies list exact local reference paths to bind; they do not embed source rows. All paths are relative to the explicit reference root, not to each policy's directory, and must pass restricted no-follow reads. Entities must match their policies and final validation spec. Unknown/duplicate keys, conflicting links, unsafe references and budget exhaustion fail closed. Source, policies, mappings, generation policies, validation and exact profile bytes bind the reviewed digest, including order and whitespace. Optional shared resource_limits supports only max_total_input_bytes and max_output_bytes ; remaining dimensions stay in per-input behavior policies. Session precedence and explicit run-cap checks below still apply. Combined review bytes must fit --max-review-bytes ; no truncation or implicit cap raise. The local create/wizard saves only policies/spec/references, not source copies or receipts. Saving changes paths and therefore requires fresh review. See the common-profile CLI workflow for draft CSV proposals, local confirmation and retained-publication restrictions. This profile is not a compatibility promise for stable 1.5.0 . The finite stable 1.6.0 campaign completed with recorded coverage limits . Registration and release acceptance grant no dataset authority or local preservation approval. Input And Generation Limits ¶ Variable Default Purpose TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_GENERATION_COUNT 100000 Maximum rows per entity TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_FILE_BYTES 134217728 Maximum bytes per input file TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_TOTAL_INPUT_BYTES 536870912 Maximum total input bytes TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_ROWS 1000000 Maximum input rows TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_COLUMNS 1000 Maximum columns TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_CELLS 10000000 Maximum row/column cells TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_FILES 100 Maximum files in a source folder TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_CELL_CHARS 1000000 Maximum characters in one CSV cell or JSON string value TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_PARQUET_EXPANDED_BYTES 536870912 Maximum estimated expanded Parquet bytes TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_YAML_ALIASES 50 Maximum YAML aliases TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_YAML_DEPTH 100 Maximum YAML nesting depth TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_JSON_DEPTH 100 Maximum structural depth for JSON datasets, profile/spec imports, and profile caches before parsing TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_BUSINESS_RULES_BYTES 1048576 Maximum rule payload bytes TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_BUSINESS_RULE_EVALUATIONS 5000000 Estimated row/rule work limit TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES 536870912 Maximum complete generated bundle size TEST_DATA_AGENT_MIN_FREE_DISK_BYTES 134217728 Disk space kept in reserve TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_GENERATION_SECONDS 300 Generation wall-clock limit TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_LOCAL_PROFILE_SECONDS 120 Wall-clock limit for one local CSV-folder profile TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_LOCAL_PROFILE_SAMPLE_ROWS 1000000 Cumulative relationship/rule sample-row ceiling per folder profile Values must be positive integers, except the two *_SECONDS values, which accept positive finite numbers. Invalid environment values fail closed. Generator MCP Invocation Deadline ¶ TEST_DATA_AGENT_MCP_MAX_INVOCATION_SECONDS defaults to 120 and accepts a finite positive number of seconds. Set it in the generator MCP client's env configuration and restart that server. The Compose generator service forwards the same variable from the shell or Compose .env file. Startup rejects invalid values with a value-free configuration error (exit 78). One captured value governs both the transport request context and service invocation; tool arguments cannot change it. For a reviewed longer run, for example set this value to 1800 . The independent TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_GENERATION_SECONDS , profiling and transformation byte/row/ cell limits still apply; set the relevant limits explicitly too. This setting does not enlarge SQL access, raw frame, argument or response-byte ceilings and does not establish measured 1M × 100 capacity. Trino MCP keeps its separate TRINO_MAX_INVOCATION_SECONDS setting. Transformation Input Limits ¶ These settings apply to transformation acquisition, decoding and policy-aware review preflight in stable 1.6.0 , plus CSV profiling/trace shape checks. They do not change source-free profiling/MCP budgets or themselves establish end-to-end capacity. Remaining pipeline caps still apply. The fictional private replacement-only CSV scenario passed 300,000 rows × 50 columns; see candidate evidence . This does not certify public execution, SQL routes or the 1M × 100 target. Use resource_limits in the saved behavior profile (not DatasetProfile): resource_limits: max_input_rows: 1000000 max_input_columns: 100 max_input_cells: 100000000 For the current shell session, override a setting explicitly: export TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_ROWS=1000000 export TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_COLUMNS=100 export TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_CELLS=100000000 For one invocation, prefix that invocation with the same NAME=value assignments instead of exporting them. No new public execution command is introduced here. In PowerShell, use $env:TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_ROWS = '1000000' for the session. Behavior-profile key under resource_limits Decoder default Unit max_input_rows 1000000 rows max_input_columns 1000 columns max_input_cells 100000000 cells max_input_file_bytes 134217728 bytes max_total_input_bytes 536870912 combined snapshot bytes max_input_cell_chars 1000000 characters max_parquet_expanded_bytes 536870912 decoded/estimated expanded bytes max_output_bytes 536870912 transformation output bytes Each key has a session variable named TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_ followed by the uppercase key. Values must be positive integers no greater than 9223372036854775807 . Precedence, per explicitly supplied field: transformation session variable, saved behavior profile, legacy TEST_DATA_AGENT_<KEY> variable, decoder default. Invalid settings fail; they are not silently ignored. Structured limit failures identify requested_above_limit or limit_exceeded , the amount, threshold, unit, and origin ( session , profile , legacy_session , or default ). They name the exact session variable and saved-profile key to change. No data values are included; no automatic increase or truncation occurs. Trace requests above the effective cell limit fail with requested_above_limit instead of being silently capped. If the trace exhausts its smaller per-run budget, limit_exceeded reports origin trace_run and explicitly names trace_csv_review_request(max_cells=...) as the parameter to increase within the session/profile ceiling. Changing only the ceiling does not change that explicit per-run argument. Registered CLI/MCP request boundaries retain typed value-free limit failures. Increasing a decoder limit does not override the explicit total-input budget, downstream work/output budgets, or explicit SQL capture run arguments. Expanded-byte accounting is not a peak-RSS promise. Transformation total-input accounting includes source, behavior policy, referenced mappings/generation policies, classification evidence and displayed review bytes. Read-only review resolves the same session/profile ceiling as the registered execution workflow; it does not silently request the default ceiling. Set TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_TOTAL_INPUT_BYTES for the session or resource_limits.max_total_input_bytes in the saved behavior profile. The registered transform-execute CLI additionally accepts --max-total-input-bytes and the workspace-scoped execute_transformation tool accepts max_total_input_bytes . These implemented RC interfaces do not issue approval. Smaller explicit run caps report snapshot_run ; a run cap above the configured ceiling is rejected, not raised. Transformation CSV character limits reach parsing, sensitivity detection and profile finalization. Internal CSV readers coordinate the stdlib process-global field limit for each record and restore its previous value even on failure. Each reader keeps its own limit; source-free readers retain legacy/default limits. External code directly changing csv.field_size_limit is outside this coordination. On parser overflow, the reported amount is the first forbidden character ( limit + 1 ), not the length of an unread remainder of the field. Transformation CSV execution uses resource_limits.max_output_bytes or TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES as the output ceiling, distinct from input-file bytes. Its explicit max_output_bytes run argument must fit that ceiling; it is no longer silently capped at 128 MiB. Actual exhaustion reports origin output_run , the encoded byte count (including CSV header and quoting), and replace_csv_snapshot(max_output_bytes=...) . Partial output is not returned. Transformation SQL/Parquet encoding checks its max_bytes run argument and reports sql_output_run / parquet_output_run with the corresponding render_transformation_sql(max_bytes=...) / render_transformation_parquet(max_bytes=...) recovery parameter. Publication also counts the manifest: bundle_run names temporary_csv_publication(max_output_bytes=...) . A bundle over budget is rejected before publication. These share the output ceiling when invoked by the publisher; standalone renderers only receive their explicit run budget. Configured query capture uses the same transformation input ceilings: max_rows / max_bytes must fit the effective row / input-file-byte limits before opening its stream. Runtime exhaustion names query_rows_run or query_bytes_run and the corresponding _capture_authorized_result argument. Captured bytes include the query envelope; decoded bytes have their own max_parquet_expanded_bytes ceiling. The resolved limits and their origins are bound into capture metadata. PostgreSQL's owned stream uses these authorized capture limits, not aggregate-profiling result-row/cell budgets; allowlists, read-only sessions and existing statement/time limits remain. The private process supervisor reconstructs only validated fixed-schema limit diagnostics after clean worker exit and cleanup, never driver exception text. The registered RC workflow uses these checks; synthetic isolation evidence does not establish live-database acceptance. The private replacement dry-run has the same checks. Its exhausted run budget reports origin replacement_trace_run and names trace_csv_replacements(max_cells=...) ; a request above the effective session/profile ceiling reports requested_above_limit before tracing. Local CSV-Folder Profile Limits ¶ Each fresh local folder profile receives one typed monotonic budget. Its defaults are 120 seconds, at most 1,000,000 retained sample rows, 536,870,912 input bytes, and 10,000,000 streamed cells. The byte and cell caps reuse TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_TOTAL_INPUT_BYTES and TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_CELLS ; the normal CLI sample is smaller at 50,000 rows via --rule-sample-rows . The Python API can pass narrower LocalProfileLimits through a fresh LocalProfileBudget . Deadline, sample, byte, or cell exhaustion raises a structured LocalProfileLimitError . A failed profile is not written to the metadata-only cache. PostgreSQL Profiling ¶ profile-postgres requires POSTGRES_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS , POSTGRES_ALLOWED_TABLES , and POSTGRES_ALLOWED_COLUMNS . Connection settings use POSTGRES_HOST , POSTGRES_PORT , POSTGRES_DATABASE , POSTGRES_USER , and POSTGRES_SSLMODE . As an alternative to the host, port, database, and TLS components, POSTGRES_JDBC_URL accepts the credential-free jdbc:postgresql://host:port/database?sslmode=verify-full shape. This is URL syntax parsed into the existing Psycopg configuration, not a Java/JDBC runtime. Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD_ENV to the name of the environment variable containing the password; never put a user or password in the URL. The URL is limited to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes, its host to 253 characters, and its database identifier to 63 characters. Each POSTGRES_ALLOWED_COLUMNS item is either an exact schema.table.column or a table-qualified schema.table.* . Wildcards are expanded from bounded metadata into explicit columns before aggregate queries; they never become SQL projection stars or local-value permissions. The POSTGRES_MAX_TABLES , POSTGRES_MAX_COLUMNS , POSTGRES_MAX_STATEMENTS , POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_ROWS , POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_CELLS , and POSTGRES_MAX_SECONDS limits bound one profile. Statement and lock timeouts use POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS and POSTGRES_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS . See the PostgreSQL workflow for a complete example. Variable Default Purpose POSTGRES_SOURCE_ID postgres Stable non-secret source identity used in qualified entity names POSTGRES_JDBC_URL unset Credential-free JDBC-style endpoint; conflicts with unequal explicit host, port, database, or TLS components POSTGRES_HOST localhost PostgreSQL host; never serialized into profile identity POSTGRES_PORT 5432 PostgreSQL port POSTGRES_DATABASE postgres Database name POSTGRES_USER test_data_agent Existing read-only database role POSTGRES_PASSWORD_ENV unset Name of the environment variable containing the password POSTGRES_SSLMODE verify-full Verify the certificate and configured hostname; weaker modes require explicit local opt-in POSTGRES_ALLOW_INSECURE false Required with require , verify-ca , or disable ; local isolated testing only POSTGRES_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS required Comma-separated schema allowlist POSTGRES_ALLOWED_TABLES required Comma-separated schema.table allowlist POSTGRES_ALLOWED_COLUMNS required Comma-separated exact schema.table.column or table-qualified schema.table.* profiling selectors POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS 30000 Per-statement timeout requested on the read-only session POSTGRES_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS 5000 Lock wait timeout requested on the read-only session POSTGRES_MAX_TABLES 100 Maximum profiled tables POSTGRES_MAX_COLUMNS 1000 Maximum profiled columns POSTGRES_MAX_STATEMENTS 1500 Cumulative statement limit POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_ROWS 10000 Cumulative aggregate/metadata result rows POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_CELLS 100000 Cumulative aggregate/metadata result cells POSTGRES_MAX_SECONDS 120 Shared monotonic profile deadline The database role must independently lack write privileges. The client also requests default_transaction_read_only=on , but that setting is defense in depth rather than a replacement for role permissions. No arbitrary SQL or source-row profiling option exists. SQL Query Source Limits ¶ profile-query uses the selected adapter's existing connection, physical table/column allowlists, statement/result/time/scan budgets, and read-only enforcement. Trino query sources require TRINO_ALLOWED_TABLE_COLUMNS ; an unrestricted Trino configuration is rejected for this command. Variable Default Purpose SQL_QUERY_MAX_BYTES 65536 Maximum UTF-8 bytes in the local query file SQL_QUERY_MAX_AST_NODES 500 Maximum parsed SQL nodes SQL_QUERY_MAX_AST_DEPTH 32 Maximum parsed SQL nesting depth SQL_QUERY_MAX_PROJECTED_COLUMNS 100 Maximum explicit fields after wildcard expansion Values must be positive integers and remain below the built-in absolute caps. The file is read once with descriptor metadata revalidation. SQL text and literals are not accepted through environment variables or CLI options and are not written to profiles, manifests, errors, providers, or MCP responses. GigaChat Advisor ¶ GigaChat is explicit and off unless agent-advise --provider gigachat is selected. Configure exactly one runtime authentication value: Variable Default Purpose GIGACHAT_CREDENTIALS unset Authorization key used by the official SDK to obtain an access token GIGACHAT_ACCESS_TOKEN unset Pre-obtained short-lived access token; mutually exclusive with GIGACHAT_CREDENTIALS GIGACHAT_SCOPE GIGACHAT_API_PERS GIGACHAT_API_PERS , GIGACHAT_API_B2B , or GIGACHAT_API_CORP GIGACHAT_CA_BUNDLE_FILE system trust store Absolute or relative path to a reviewed readable CA bundle Credentials are never accepted as CLI arguments or written to settings, workspaces, logs, or errors. The API and authorization endpoints are fixed to the official HTTPS services. TLS verification cannot be disabled; endpoint, client-certificate, SSL-context, or token-expiry overrides fail locally. The CLI exposes only the optional --model override. Applications that use the Python adapter can provide frozen GigaChatAdvisorSettings to narrow the default 4 MiB request, 1 MiB response, 4,096 output-token, 15-second timeout, and zero-retry budgets. See Use The GigaChat Advisor . Generator MCP ¶ See MCP Permissions for the tool-by-tool rights matrix. These settings constrain application behavior; they do not grant operating-system access, database privileges or human approval. Ordinary MCP tool paths use the workspace; audit/authentication files and owned runtime temporary storage have separate configured locations. Variable Required Purpose TEST_DATA_AGENT_WORKSPACE_ROOT Recommended Bounds generator workspace tool paths; does not sandbox the process or relocate audit/authentication/runtime temporary files TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_PROFILE_PAYLOAD_BYTES Optional Maximum inline safe profile size; defaults to 4 MiB TEST_DATA_AGENT_AUDIT_LOG Optional Enables a shared HMAC-authenticated JSONL audit log TEST_DATA_AGENT_AUDIT_HMAC_KEY Required with audit log Base64 key containing at least 32 random bytes TEST_DATA_AGENT_AUDIT_HMAC_KEY_FILE Alternative to key value Path to a bounded base64 secret file TEST_DATA_AGENT_AUDIT_ACTOR Optional Stable non-sensitive worker or deployment label TEST_DATA_AGENT_AUDIT_MAX_BYTES Optional Audit log size limit; defaults to 64 MiB When unset, the generator server uses the current working directory. For shared or production-like use, always set a dedicated narrow workspace. Configure exactly one of TEST_DATA_AGENT_AUDIT_HMAC_KEY and TEST_DATA_AGENT_AUDIT_HMAC_KEY_FILE . Secret files must be regular, non-linked, at most 4096 bytes, and not group- or world-writable. Trino MCP ¶ The default aggregate-only tools are source-literal-free. The explicit opt-in row-returning tools are configured separately. Both servers use stdio, with no MCP HTTP listener or per-tool OAuth scopes. Trino database authentication and client tool-confirmation policy remain separate: Variable Default Purpose TRINO_ENABLE_SAFE_SELECT false Enables run_safe_select ; every returned string is recursively masked in bounded composite values, but other non-string source values may remain outside the source-literal-free guarantee Trino Connection ¶ Use TRINO_JDBC_URL as an alternative to separate host and port settings. Its supported form is jdbc:trino://host:port/catalog/schema?SSL=true . Catalog and schema are optional request defaults and are accepted only when each is in the mandatory allowlist. Authentication remains in TRINO_USER and existing runtime secret mechanisms; URL credentials, tokens, roles, session properties, headers, proxies, unknown properties, and SSL=false are rejected. The URL is parsed into the existing Python Trino client and does not load Java or a JDBC driver. The URL is limited to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes, its host to 253 characters, and each catalog or schema identifier to 255 characters. For a complete MCP username/password configuration, including protected password injection and a macOS Keychain launcher, follow MCP with a username and password or the Russian guide . Variable Default Purpose TRINO_JDBC_URL unset Credential-free JDBC-style endpoint; conflicts with unequal explicit endpoint/default components TRINO_HOST localhost Trino host name TRINO_PORT 8080 Trino port TRINO_USER test_data_agent Trino user TRINO_HTTP_SCHEME https https or explicitly allowed http TRINO_AUTH_METHOD none Optional methods in stable 1.6.0 : basic , jwt , kerberos , gssapi , oauth2 , certificate ; authenticated connections require HTTPS and certificate verification TRINO_AUTH_SECRET_ENV unset Name of a runtime environment variable containing the Basic password or JWT, not the secret itself TRINO_AUTH_CERTIFICATE_ENV unset Name of a runtime environment variable containing the client certificate path TRINO_AUTH_KEY_ENV unset Name of a runtime environment variable containing the private-key path TRINO_CATALOG unset Optional request default; must be in TRINO_ALLOWED_CATALOGS TRINO_SCHEMA unset Optional request default; requires TRINO_CATALOG and membership in TRINO_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS TRINO_ALLOWED_CATALOGS required Comma-separated catalog allowlist TRINO_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS required Comma-separated schema allowlist TRINO_ALLOWED_TABLE_COLUMNS unset Optional exact catalog.schema.table.column or restricted table-qualified catalog.schema.table.* profile selectors; wildcard does not authorize category literals TRINO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 30 Client request timeout, 0.1 to 300 TRINO_MAX_RESULT_ROWS 10000 Client result cap, maximum 100000 TRINO_QUERY_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME 30s Trino execution-time session budget TRINO_QUERY_MAX_RUN_TIME 45s Trino total run-time session budget TRINO_QUERY_MAX_SCAN_PHYSICAL_BYTES 1GB Trino physical scan budget TRINO_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE trusted-local trusted-local permits an unset cumulative scan ceiling; shared-hardened requires a finite TRINO_MAX_INVOCATION_ESTIMATED_SCAN_BYTES The Kerberos/GSSAPI methods require their driver's optional requests_kerberos / requests_gssapi dependencies and existing runtime credentials. They use mutual authentication without delegation. profile-query --adapter trino --trino-oauth-browser explicitly opts into opening the configured Trino HTTPS authentication route at a local terminal when TRINO_AUTH_METHOD=oauth2 . It never prints authentication URLs; pipes reject before connection. This is a local-only flag; MCP never installs a browser callback. Python applications can explicitly supply their own trusted redirect callback. The auth object is reused within one client; OAuth token caching remains the driver's implementation, including its optional operating-system keyring backend. These local checks do not prove remote reachability or authorize live access. The OAuth2 HTTP adapter also guards the driver's direct token polling: requests must target the configured HTTPS Trino host and port, use verified TLS, and fit the remaining invocation/request deadline. Environment proxies and netrc are not inherited. Other token-server origins fail closed; this is not evidence of acceptance against a remote identity provider or a hard wall-clock guarantee for arbitrary slow response bodies. Selecting OAuth2 installs idempotent value-free diagnostic filters on trino.auth and urllib3.connectionpool ; the latter can log token request paths at DEBUG. These filters remain attached for the process lifetime, including other traffic using those loggers. They neither store secrets nor disable the process logger or change its level. Duration values use ms , s , m , or h . Data-size values use B , kB , MB , or GB . TRINO_QUERY_MAX_RUN_TIME must be greater than or equal to TRINO_QUERY_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME . When TRINO_ALLOWED_TABLE_COLUMNS is set, table profiling uses only its exact selectors plus metadata-expanded columns from a matching table wildcard. The request fails before aggregate work when metadata is empty, malformed, duplicated, inconsistent, or over the invocation column budget. This selector is not a universal per-tool ACL: metadata discovery, count/cardinality tools, rule probes and optional run_safe_select do not apply it. The optional row tool checks catalog/schema scope and SQL safety, not this column list. Restrict the database identity's actual table/column grants independently. Catalog and schema allowlists are independent sets, not allowed catalog/schema pairs. See Trino tool rights . Trino Invocation Limits ¶ These limits apply to one MCP tool invocation, including nested table and column profiling. Every invocation receives a fresh monotonic budget. Variable Default Unit Scope Failure behavior TRINO_MAX_INVOCATION_PROFILED_COLUMNS 100 columns Per invocation Rejects before profiling the next column TRINO_MAX_INVOCATION_STATEMENTS 150 statements Per invocation Rejects before opening the next Trino connection TRINO_MAX_INVOCATION_SECONDS 120 seconds Per invocation Clamps HTTP and Trino query timeouts; closes active query resources on expiry TRINO_MAX_INVOCATION_ESTIMATED_SCAN_BYTES unset bytes Per invocation; required for shared-hardened Rejects before a statement whose conservative estimate would exceed the limit All configured values must be finite and positive. Column, statement, and scan limits accept integers; invocation seconds accepts a number. Invalid values fail server startup. The shared-hardened profile fails closed when the cumulative scan ceiling is unset. Budget exhaustion raises a bounded query-work error and does not restore work already consumed by nested helpers. The typed budget also keeps database_result_bytes and transport_response_bytes separate; each defaults to 4 MiB in the Trino MCP work limits. The transport limit is measured in UTF-8 bytes after final MCP JSON serialization and framing, at the production writer boundary. Its minimum is 350 bytes: that fixed amount is reserved for the bounded terminal error response, so normal responses can use at most the configured total minus the reserve. A related notification and its final response share the same per-invocation budget. TRINO_QUERY_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME , TRINO_QUERY_MAX_RUN_TIME , and TRINO_QUERY_MAX_SCAN_PHYSICAL_BYTES remain per-query limits. The invocation deadline clamps the two per-query time limits and TRINO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to the remaining invocation time. When the optional cumulative scan limit is set, each statement conservatively consumes the configured per-query TRINO_QUERY_MAX_SCAN_PHYSICAL_BYTES cap. Leaving the cumulative cap unset is allowed only for the explicitly named trusted-local profile; the shared-hardened profile requires a finite cap before startup. Explicit Safety Overrides ¶ Variable Default Effect TRINO_ALLOW_UNRESTRICTED false Allows missing catalog/schema allowlists TRINO_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP false Allows plain HTTP These accept 1 , true , yes , or on and their false equivalents. Do not enable either override for production or production-adjacent Trino. Plain HTTP is intended only for an isolated local integration environment. Configured SQL Session Bounds ¶ The generator MCP entrypoint reads these administrator settings once at startup. They bound the instance-owned configured_query_session manager, not ordinary source-free profiling or database credentials. Published 1.5.0 has no session tool. Invalid settings or workspace paths stop startup with a fixed error and exit code 78. Variable Default Accepted values and meaning TEST_DATA_AGENT_QUERY_SESSION_MAX_ACTIVE 4 Integer 1–32; maximum simultaneously owned sessions. TEST_DATA_AGENT_QUERY_SESSION_MAX_CUMULATIVE_BYTES 67108864 Positive integer through 9223372036854775807; lifetime input-byte reservation ceiling for this server instance. TEST_DATA_AGENT_QUERY_SESSION_MAX_SECONDS 300 Finite seconds 0.1–3600; session lifetime starts before capture and is never renewed by requests. Each open reserves its explicit max_total_bytes before database work. Reservations are not refunded after failure, close or expiry. Per-input policy and transformation session ceilings still apply, as do SQL allowlists and statement, scan, invocation, transport and response budgets. Active operations are clamped to the session's remaining lifetime and request deadline. max_review_bytes must be positive and no greater than max_total_bytes ; the output cap must fit the effective batch output ceiling. Expiry timers clean owned snapshots without requiring another request. The entrypoint also closes all sessions on normal or failed transport shutdown; cleanup failures refuse further work. See the session workflow .

docs.text: English · Русский Defaults are conservative. Raise limits only after reviewing expected data volume, available resources, and the trust level of the input. These settings describe stable 1.6.0 . Historical anchors remain available. Configuration and tool registration do not grant dataset permission or local preservation approval. Existing component settings and exact allowlists remain supported. All byte values are integer bytes unless stated otherwise. CLI flags override the corresponding command defaults. Environment variables configure resource, database, provider, and transport boundaries only where listed below; they do not silently activate an optional provider or overwrite an explicit CLI value. Use COMMAND --help to inspect CLI defaults and doctor --json for installed/local capability states. doctor deliberately does not read provider credentials or test remote reachability.
docs.title: Configuration

docs.text: Stable 1.6.0 provides the common CLI/MCP workflow. Its versioned reference profile combines two or more inputs with one independently reviewed DatasetSpec for final linked validation: schema_version: "0.1" validation: validation.yaml inputs: - entity: fictional_parents source: parents.csv policy: parents-policy.yaml - entity: fictional_children source: children.csv policy: children-policy.yaml mappings: [keys.csv] mappings and generation_policies list exact local reference paths to bind; they do not embed source rows. All paths are relative to the explicit reference root, not to each policy's directory, and must pass restricted no-follow reads. Entities must match their policies and final validation spec. Unknown/duplicate keys, conflicting links, unsafe references and budget exhaustion fail closed. Source, policies, mappings, generation policies, validation and exact profile bytes bind the reviewed digest, including order and whitespace. Optional shared resource_limits supports only max_total_input_bytes and max_output_bytes ; remaining dimensions stay in per-input behavior policies. Session precedence and explicit run-cap checks below still apply. Combined review bytes must fit --max-review-bytes ; no truncation or implicit cap raise. The local create/wizard saves only policies/spec/references, not source copies or receipts. Saving changes paths and therefore requires fresh review. See the common-profile CLI workflow for draft CSV proposals, local confirmation and retained-publication restrictions. This profile is not a compatibility promise for stable 1.5.0 . The finite stable 1.6.0 campaign completed with recorded coverage limits . Registration and release acceptance grant no dataset authority or local preservation approval.

docs.text: TEST_DATA_AGENT_MCP_MAX_INVOCATION_SECONDS defaults to 120 and accepts a finite positive number of seconds. Set it in the generator MCP client's env configuration and restart that server. The Compose generator service forwards the same variable from the shell or Compose .env file. Startup rejects invalid values with a value-free configuration error (exit 78). One captured value governs both the transport request context and service invocation; tool arguments cannot change it. For a reviewed longer run, for example set this value to 1800 . The independent TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_GENERATION_SECONDS , profiling and transformation byte/row/ cell limits still apply; set the relevant limits explicitly too. This setting does not enlarge SQL access, raw frame, argument or response-byte ceilings and does not establish measured 1M × 100 capacity. Trino MCP keeps its separate TRINO_MAX_INVOCATION_SECONDS setting.
docs.title: Generator MCP Invocation Deadline

docs.text: These settings apply to transformation acquisition, decoding and policy-aware review preflight in stable 1.6.0 , plus CSV profiling/trace shape checks. They do not change source-free profiling/MCP budgets or themselves establish end-to-end capacity. Remaining pipeline caps still apply. The fictional private replacement-only CSV scenario passed 300,000 rows × 50 columns; see candidate evidence . This does not certify public execution, SQL routes or the 1M × 100 target. Use resource_limits in the saved behavior profile (not DatasetProfile): resource_limits: max_input_rows: 1000000 max_input_columns: 100 max_input_cells: 100000000 For the current shell session, override a setting explicitly: export TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_ROWS=1000000 export TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_COLUMNS=100 export TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_CELLS=100000000 For one invocation, prefix that invocation with the same NAME=value assignments instead of exporting them. No new public execution command is introduced here. In PowerShell, use $env:TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_INPUT_ROWS = '1000000' for the session. Behavior-profile key under resource_limits Decoder default Unit max_input_rows 1000000 rows max_input_columns 1000 columns max_input_cells 100000000 cells max_input_file_bytes 134217728 bytes max_total_input_bytes 536870912 combined snapshot bytes max_input_cell_chars 1000000 characters max_parquet_expanded_bytes 536870912 decoded/estimated expanded bytes max_output_bytes 536870912 transformation output bytes Each key has a session variable named TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_ followed by the uppercase key. Values must be positive integers no greater than 9223372036854775807 . Precedence, per explicitly supplied field: transformation session variable, saved behavior profile, legacy TEST_DATA_AGENT_<KEY> variable, decoder default. Invalid settings fail; they are not silently ignored. Structured limit failures identify requested_above_limit or limit_exceeded , the amount, threshold, unit, and origin ( session , profile , legacy_session , or default ). They name the exact session variable and saved-profile key to change. No data values are included; no automatic increase or truncation occurs. Trace requests above the effective cell limit fail with requested_above_limit instead of being silently capped. If the trace exhausts its smaller per-run budget, limit_exceeded reports origin trace_run and explicitly names trace_csv_review_request(max_cells=...) as the parameter to increase within the session/profile ceiling. Changing only the ceiling does not change that explicit per-run argument. Registered CLI/MCP request boundaries retain typed value-free limit failures. Increasing a decoder limit does not override the explicit total-input budget, downstream work/output budgets, or explicit SQL capture run arguments. Expanded-byte accounting is not a peak-RSS promise. Transformation total-input accounting includes source, behavior policy, referenced mappings/generation policies, classification evidence and displayed review bytes. Read-only review resolves the same session/profile ceiling as the registered execution workflow; it does not silently request the default ceiling. Set TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_TOTAL_INPUT_BYTES for the session or resource_limits.max_total_input_bytes in the saved behavior profile. The registered transform-execute CLI additionally accepts --max-total-input-bytes and the workspace-scoped execute_transformation tool accepts max_total_input_bytes . These implemented RC interfaces do not issue approval. Smaller explicit run caps report snapshot_run ; a run cap above the configured ceiling is rejected, not raised. Transformation CSV character limits reach parsing, sensitivity detection and profile finalization. Internal CSV readers coordinate the stdlib process-global field limit for each record and restore its previous value even on failure. Each reader keeps its own limit; source-free readers retain legacy/default limits. External code directly changing csv.field_size_limit is outside this coordination. On parser overflow, the reported amount is the first forbidden character ( limit + 1 ), not the length of an unread remainder of the field. Transformation CSV execution uses resource_limits.max_output_bytes or TEST_DATA_AGENT_TRANSFORM_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES as the output ceiling, distinct from input-file bytes. Its explicit max_output_bytes run argument must fit that ceiling; it is no longer silently capped at 128 MiB. Actual exhaustion reports origin output_run , the encoded byte count (including CSV header and quoting), and replace_csv_snapshot(max_output_bytes=...) . Partial output is not returned. Transformation SQL/Parquet encoding checks its max_bytes run argument and reports sql_output_run / parquet_output_run with the corresponding render_transformation_sql(max_bytes=...) / render_transformation_parquet(max_bytes=...) recovery parameter. Publication also counts the manifest: bundle_run names temporary_csv_publication(max_output_bytes=...) . A bundle over budget is rejected before publication. These share the output ceiling when invoked by the publisher; standalone renderers only receive their explicit run budget. Configured query capture uses the same transformation input ceilings: max_rows / max_bytes must fit the effective row / input-file-byte limits before opening its stream. Runtime exhaustion names query_rows_run or query_bytes_run and the corresponding _capture_authorized_result argument. Captured bytes include the query envelope; decoded bytes have their own max_parquet_expanded_bytes ceiling. The resolved limits and their origins are bound into capture metadata. PostgreSQL's owned stream uses these authorized capture limits, not aggregate-profiling result-row/cell budgets; allowlists, read-only sessions and existing statement/time limits remain. The private process supervisor reconstructs only validated fixed-schema limit diagnostics after clean worker exit and cleanup, never driver exception text. The registered RC workflow uses these checks; synthetic isolation evidence does not establish live-database acceptance. The private replacement dry-run has the same checks. Its exhausted run budget reports origin replacement_trace_run and names trace_csv_replacements(max_cells=...) ; a request above the effective session/profile ceiling reports requested_above_limit before tracing.

docs.text: Each fresh local folder profile receives one typed monotonic budget. Its defaults are 120 seconds, at most 1,000,000 retained sample rows, 536,870,912 input bytes, and 10,000,000 streamed cells. The byte and cell caps reuse TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_TOTAL_INPUT_BYTES and TEST_DATA_AGENT_MAX_INPUT_CELLS ; the normal CLI sample is smaller at 50,000 rows via --rule-sample-rows . The Python API can pass narrower LocalProfileLimits through a fresh LocalProfileBudget . Deadline, sample, byte, or cell exhaustion raises a structured LocalProfileLimitError . A failed profile is not written to the metadata-only cache.

docs.text: profile-postgres requires POSTGRES_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS , POSTGRES_ALLOWED_TABLES , and POSTGRES_ALLOWED_COLUMNS . Connection settings use POSTGRES_HOST , POSTGRES_PORT , POSTGRES_DATABASE , POSTGRES_USER , and POSTGRES_SSLMODE . As an alternative to the host, port, database, and TLS components, POSTGRES_JDBC_URL accepts the credential-free jdbc:postgresql://host:port/database?sslmode=verify-full shape. This is URL syntax parsed into the existing Psycopg configuration, not a Java/JDBC runtime. Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD_ENV to the name of the environment variable containing the password; never put a user or password in the URL. The URL is limited to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes, its host to 253 characters, and its database identifier to 63 characters. Each POSTGRES_ALLOWED_COLUMNS item is either an exact schema.table.column or a table-qualified schema.table.* . Wildcards are expanded from bounded metadata into explicit columns before aggregate queries; they never become SQL projection stars or local-value permissions. The POSTGRES_MAX_TABLES , POSTGRES_MAX_COLUMNS , POSTGRES_MAX_STATEMENTS , POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_ROWS , POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_CELLS , and POSTGRES_MAX_SECONDS limits bound one profile. Statement and lock timeouts use POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS and POSTGRES_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS . See the PostgreSQL workflow for a complete example. Variable Default Purpose POSTGRES_SOURCE_ID postgres Stable non-secret source identity used in qualified entity names POSTGRES_JDBC_URL unset Credential-free JDBC-style endpoint; conflicts with unequal explicit host, port, database, or TLS components POSTGRES_HOST localhost PostgreSQL host; never serialized into profile identity POSTGRES_PORT 5432 PostgreSQL port POSTGRES_DATABASE postgres Database name POSTGRES_USER test_data_agent Existing read-only database role POSTGRES_PASSWORD_ENV unset Name of the environment variable containing the password POSTGRES_SSLMODE verify-full Verify the certificate and configured hostname; weaker modes require explicit local opt-in POSTGRES_ALLOW_INSECURE false Required with require , verify-ca , or disable ; local isolated testing only POSTGRES_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS required Comma-separated schema allowlist POSTGRES_ALLOWED_TABLES required Comma-separated schema.table allowlist POSTGRES_ALLOWED_COLUMNS required Comma-separated exact schema.table.column or table-qualified schema.table.* profiling selectors POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS 30000 Per-statement timeout requested on the read-only session POSTGRES_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS 5000 Lock wait timeout requested on the read-only session POSTGRES_MAX_TABLES 100 Maximum profiled tables POSTGRES_MAX_COLUMNS 1000 Maximum profiled columns POSTGRES_MAX_STATEMENTS 1500 Cumulative statement limit POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_ROWS 10000 Cumulative aggregate/metadata result rows POSTGRES_MAX_RESULT_CELLS 100000 Cumulative aggregate/metadata result cells POSTGRES_MAX_SECONDS 120 Shared monotonic profile deadline The database role must independently lack write privileges. The client also requests default_transaction_read_only=on , but that setting is defense in depth rather than a replacement for role permissions. No arbitrary SQL or source-row profiling option exists.

docs.text: profile-query uses the selected adapter's existing connection, physical table/column allowlists, statement/result/time/scan budgets, and read-only enforcement. Trino query sources require TRINO_ALLOWED_TABLE_COLUMNS ; an unrestricted Trino configuration is rejected for this command. Variable Default Purpose SQL_QUERY_MAX_BYTES 65536 Maximum UTF-8 bytes in the local query file SQL_QUERY_MAX_AST_NODES 500 Maximum parsed SQL nodes SQL_QUERY_MAX_AST_DEPTH 32 Maximum parsed SQL nesting depth SQL_QUERY_MAX_PROJECTED_COLUMNS 100 Maximum explicit fields after wildcard expansion Values must be positive integers and remain below the built-in absolute caps. The file is read once with descriptor metadata revalidation. SQL text and literals are not accepted through environment variables or CLI options and are not written to profiles, manifests, errors, providers, or MCP responses.

docs.text: GigaChat is explicit and off unless agent-advise --provider gigachat is selected. Configure exactly one runtime authentication value: Variable Default Purpose GIGACHAT_CREDENTIALS unset Authorization key used by the official SDK to obtain an access token GIGACHAT_ACCESS_TOKEN unset Pre-obtained short-lived access token; mutually exclusive with GIGACHAT_CREDENTIALS GIGACHAT_SCOPE GIGACHAT_API_PERS GIGACHAT_API_PERS , GIGACHAT_API_B2B , or GIGACHAT_API_CORP GIGACHAT_CA_BUNDLE_FILE system trust store Absolute or relative path to a reviewed readable CA bundle Credentials are never accepted as CLI arguments or written to settings, workspaces, logs, or errors. The API and authorization endpoints are fixed to the official HTTPS services. TLS verification cannot be disabled; endpoint, client-certificate, SSL-context, or token-expiry overrides fail locally. The CLI exposes only the optional --model override. Applications that use the Python adapter can provide frozen GigaChatAdvisorSettings to narrow the default 4 MiB request, 1 MiB response, 4,096 output-token, 15-second timeout, and zero-retry budgets. See Use The GigaChat Advisor .

docs.text: See MCP Permissions for the tool-by-tool rights matrix. These settings constrain application behavior; they do not grant operating-system access, database privileges or human approval. Ordinary MCP tool paths use the workspace; audit/authentication files and owned runtime temporary storage have separate configured locations. docs.text: The default aggregate-only tools are source-literal-free. The explicit opt-in row-returning tools are configured separately. Both servers use stdio, with no MCP HTTP listener or per-tool OAuth scopes. docs.text: Use TRINO_JDBC_URL as an alternative to separate host and port settings. Its supported form is jdbc:trino://host:port/catalog/schema?SSL=true . Catalog and schema are optional request defaults and are accepted only when each is in the mandatory allowlist. Authentication remains in TRINO_USER and existing runtime secret mechanisms; URL credentials, tokens, roles, session properties, headers, proxies, unknown properties, and SSL=false are rejected. The URL is parsed into the existing Python Trino client and does not load Java or a JDBC driver. The URL is limited to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes, its host to 253 characters, and each catalog or schema identifier to 255 characters. For a complete MCP username/password configuration, including protected password injection and a macOS Keychain launcher, follow MCP with a username and password or the Russian guide . TEST_DATA_AGENT_QUERY_SESSION_MAX_SECONDS 300 Finite seconds 0.1–3600; session lifetime starts before capture and is never renewed by requests. docs.text: Generation Contract Corrections ¶ English · Русский These corrections are included in stable 1.6.0 . Regenerate affected fixtures and review differences when upgrading. Package version and DatasetSpec schema version are separate; the current specification schema is 1.1 . Changed Results ¶ Formula dependencies are computed before their consumers, regardless of list order. Cycles and multiple assignments to the same formula target fail early. Constraints and relationships marked rejected are ignored by generation and validation. Existing inferred rules in an explicitly supplied specification remain executable; the agent workflow still requires fingerprint approval. Remove or revise active aggregate mappings that depend on a rejected link; they fail validation instead of being silently skipped. Nullable foreign keys preserve generated nulls. One-to-one capacity counts only non-null child references. Required identifiers cannot be empty or null. String-pattern lengths describe the entire string, including any synthetic prefix. Short non-sensitive strings use random characters where a prefix does not fit. A required string cannot have a zero maximum length. Regenerate affected fixtures and review resulting differences. A fixed seed remains reproducible within the recorded generator version and environment; it does not promise identical bytes across this upgrade. Publication And Validation ¶ Valid, edge, and load-test generation must pass all core schema, relationship, constraint, and privacy checks before returning rows or publishing output. Turning off report sections does not disable these generation checks. Business rule mutations are checked again before publication. Failures preserve existing output and do not publish a new successful bundle. Explicit mixed and negative generation still publish controlled-invalid data with validation evidence. Parquet uses explicitly marked scalar columns when intentionally malformed cells cannot fit native Arrow types. The bundle reader restores those cells for validation; consumers reading Parquet directly must inspect the apa.scalar_encoding field metadata. Ordinary valid-mode values incompatible with declared types still reject the whole export without partial publication. Row privacy remains mandatory in every mode. The RC5 CLI reports validation_failed with exit 1 for intentionally invalid results while retaining the representable output, manifest and report. Explicit mode/ratio overrides must be reflected in effective execution evidence; an invalid artifact is not a successful validation. Standalone validate now inspects row values when its privacy section is enabled, in addition to checking specification safety. CSV numeric values are interpreted using their declared numeric type before privacy classification. This decoding exception applies to revalidation only; generated formula and business-rule strings retain the strict pre-export privacy check. These checks detect recognizable sensitive strings using the existing synthetic namespace policy. They do not certify anonymity or prove that data has never come from a source. Keep the source-row checks and organization-specific review. The solver does not search for a solution to arbitrary interacting rules. If later temporal, conditional, or aggregate changes invalidate an earlier rule, the operation fails; revise the specification rather than consuming partial output. Numeric sampling remains uniform between configured bounds and foreign key assignment remains round-robin among non-null child rows. These are not claims of preserving correlations or source fan-out distributions. Additive validation utility evidence ¶ New reports add utility with the canonical effective-spec hash, active native relationship/temporal declaration counts and executed/not-declared/not-run status. Temporal metrics add generated checked/failing row counts. Existing validity, settings, section errors and relationship metrics retain their semantics. Old saved reports without utility remain accepted. JSON consumers that enforce exact keys must admit this new optional field. Generated row values, DatasetSpec versions and existing profile/spec hashes are unchanged. Serialized validation reports and their manifest output digests do change. Compare replayed rows separately from report byte identity across this upgrade; the new contract fixtures record the intentional report changes. Unknown source fidelity, fan-out and missing relationship coverage remain unknown. No source queries, new authorization, dependency, package publication or completed release-candidate acceptance is implied. Parquet distinctness evidence ¶ Reprofile Parquet sources to obtain bounded non-null distinctness. Old profiles retain unknown values. Newly profiled scalar columns may have exact or lower_bound unique-ratio evidence using existing schema fields; changed profile fingerprints require fresh plan review. This adds no primary-key nomination, identifier pool or source key reuse. Missing null metadata still blocks automatic spec inference. Existing dataset/profile schema versions remain unchanged. Long fractional datetime intervals ¶ Datetime range sampling now computes its whole-second span with integer arithmetic. Very long fractional intervals previously could round the maximum admissible offset up and exceed the upper bound by a microsecond. Replaying such an affected specification may produce different values after upgrading; compare the manifest's generator version. The existing second-resolution policy, missing-bound fallbacks and schema version are unchanged. This does not add monthly/calendar inference or certify source-period fidelity. A partial date/time bound must also be compatible with the existing missing endpoint defaults (minimum 2020-01-01, maximum 2025-01-01). A maximum before 2020 or minimum after 2025 now rejects instead of silently clamping an inverted interval. Supply both ordered bounds for earlier or later periods. Failure leaves previous dataset artifacts unchanged and publishes no new manifest. CSV numeric replacement evidence ¶ Reprofile CSV folders to replace cache format 7 with format 8. Ambiguous numeric phone-like fields may now include optional numeric_storage_type ; sensitivity and masked patterns are unchanged. Old ambiguous profiles cannot opt into a numeric replacement without fresh storage evidence. Independently authored numeric_measure decimal ranges use the existing infer-spec --decimal-fields contract. Re-review changed profile/spec fingerprints. In an awaiting-approval workspace, copy the reviewed field while preserving planned generation settings, run agent-review and approve the new fingerprint. Do not mutate an already approved plan; replan changed source/profile evidence. DatasetSpec version 1.1 and unaffected legacy hashes remain unchanged; see profiling . Query-summary batching ¶ Query-source summary batching changes trusted internal SQL and request counts, not profile/spec schemas. Fixed aggregate evidence keeps the same profile fingerprint; there is no silent reclassification or saved-plan promotion. Existing statement, scan, result and time limits remain enforced independently. Real source changes still require normal profile review. Optional conditional formulas ¶ Formula rules add optional when with the existing typed Condition semantics. Absent/null predicates serialize as omitted and retain prior hashes and seeded behavior. Reports add eligible/evaluated/skipped counters only for conditional formulas; strict consumers should accept these additive counters. DatasetSpec stays at 1.1. Reviewed conditional branches change the rules/spec fingerprint and require renewed plan review. Conditional writer conflicts reject before publication; no existing source access or privacy permission is expanded.

docs.text: Generation modes and folder replacement ¶ English · Русский These modes are available in stable 1.6.0 . edge generates valid lower and upper numeric/decimal/date/time bounds, zero when in range, both allowed booleans, all declared categories and string length boundaries. Numeric bounds include the declared scale_factor , as in normal generation. Nullable fields with a positive null ratio include null cases. Identifiers remain synthetic; constraint solving preserves declared uniqueness, foreign keys, formulas and business rules, which can replace a field boundary when it conflicts with another invariant. Row count stays unchanged: small outputs cannot cover every boundary. Sensitive string fields retain safe synthetic providers rather than source values. No invalid values are intentional. load_test multiplies each entity's requested row count by generation_settings.load_multiplier (default 10). Explicit CLI --count or Python bundle count supplies the exact row count without multiplication. Direct generate-from-csv and generate --profile require an explicit count and use it exactly. The generate-from-example folder shortcut permits an omitted count and then uses the inferred per-entity profile counts; use a reviewed DatasetSpec to select load_test for that staged workflow. Generation remains seeded and valid; all row, payload, disk and execution budgets apply before allocation. An oversized request fails rather than truncates. This mode produces data for load testing; it does not send traffic or run a benchmark. valid , edge and load_test reject a nonzero --invalid-ratio . Omit --invalid-ratio for these modes (an explicit zero is also accepted), or select mixed / negative when invalid values are intentional. Rejected combinations exit 2 before publishing output; they do not modify the input specification. DatasetSpec generate --overwrite replaces the entire destination folder, including obsolete files. Without the flag, nonempty folders are rejected. Generation, rules and validation finish before replacing existing output. A sibling staging directory and previous-folder backup permit rollback on publication failure. Directory replacement has a brief rename interval; it is not a concurrent-reader atomic exchange. Do not modify the destination concurrently. Symlinks and an output folder containing the input specification are rejected. An interruption or a failure removing the previous folder can leave a hidden .rollback folder; retain it until recovery is complete. Single-file generation keeps its existing bundle-replacement contract. Transformation permissions do not change. The default load_multiplier is omitted from serialization to preserve existing specification fingerprints. Custom multipliers and materialized exact-count specs change fingerprints and require fresh plan review. Replaying a seeded run ¶ Keep the same seed, ordered specification, generation settings, business rules, package version and dependency environment when replaying a run. Identifiers remain synthetic; constraint solving preserves declared uniqueness, foreign keys, formulas and business rules, which can replace a field boundary when it conflicts with another invariant. docs.text: MCP Permissions ¶ Use this reference to decide which MCP tools a client may call and which local resources each server process needs. Start with the generator-only quickstart . The tables describe stable 1.6.0 ; installed versions can expose fewer tools. Check the installed version and its tools/list response. Discovery is an inventory, not authorization to use a dataset or activate a gated transformation extension. Who Grants Access ¶ Layer Who configures it What it controls MCP client Client operator Whether the assistant can discover/call a server's tools and when the client asks for confirmation. Use the client's tool allow/ask controls, if supported. Operating system or container Deployment administrator Executable launch, readable inputs, writable outputs and temporary storage, readable secrets, and network destinations. Run as a dedicated non-root user. Application configuration Server administrator Generator workspace, Trino allowlists, optional row-tool registration, and work/response budgets. Tool arguments cannot widen these settings. Database Database administrator Authentication, metadata visibility, and read-only access to selected tables/columns. Application allowlists do not create database grants. Workflow review Human reviewer Approval of the exact synthetic specification; separate local controlling-terminal approval for preservation. A client permission to call a tool does not supply either review. Both installed server commands use stdio . The client launches a local process and exchanges MCP messages on its standard input/output. No listening HTTP port, inbound firewall rule, remote MCP login, or MCP OAuth scope is required. These entrypoints do not implement a remote authorization server or publish per-tool OAuth scopes or permission annotations. Configure permissions in the actual client and deployment; do not invent a permissions or scopes key in the server configuration. Trino authentication is a separate outbound database connection, not authentication of an MCP caller. Client confirmation rules apply in that client. They do not restrict a different client or grant an operating-system sandbox. The normal server does not provide a configurable per-tool authorization list; TRINO_ENABLE_SAFE_SELECT controls the separate optional row tool. For a hard isolation boundary, use dedicated process credentials and the separate container deployments . Default Trino profiling Installed runtime and any administrator-selected TLS/authentication files Runtime temporary storage; separate audit directory only if enabled Outbound access to the configured Trino endpoint; a restricted read-only database identity. No generator workspace mount is needed. Local selective transformation Workspace source snapshots, policies, mappings, and any existing local receipt New selected output bundle and owned temporary storage/cleanup No database or provider connection is needed for local-file operations. Preservation requires separate local approval. Configured SQL transformation session Workspace batch profile, bounded query-reference/query files, policies/mappings; configured connection secrets Private owned temporary captures/receipts and selected output bundle Authorized PostgreSQL or Trino connection, optional adapter dependencies and read-only grants. This is a separate row-capture workflow, not aggregate-only profiling. Optional audit logging, either server The selected HMAC key or key file Create/append the selected log in its existing private parent directory No network required. Use different keys and directories for separate workers. TEST_DATA_AGENT_WORKSPACE_ROOT must point to an existing dedicated directory. If unset, the generator uses its current working directory. Generator tool paths must resolve below the root; relative paths are easiest to audit. Escapes through existing symlinks are rejected. The setting restricts application tool paths; it does not remove the process user's rights to other host files. Audit paths, authentication files and owned runtime temporary storage have their own administrator-configured locations and are not ordinary workspace tool paths. Keep secrets outside the client-accessible workspace. Grant read/traverse access to selected inputs and write/traverse access only to the required workspace/output and temporary directories. The server must also be able to remove its own temporary files. Root, sudo, access to the user's whole home directory, and a Docker socket inside the worker are unnecessary. The normal MCP generation tools refuse existing output files and non-empty output folders; they have no folder-overwrite argument. CLI --overwrite does not grant MCP overwrite permission. The shipped generator Compose service has no network or database dependencies. Keep that setup for synthetic/local-file work. It cannot perform configured SQL capture; that separately accepted workflow needs an explicitly provisioned deployment, not a silent change to the generator-only setup. Generator Tool Rights ¶ All file references below are workspace-confined, except the server-owned temporary session storage described above. Responses contain summaries, reports and artifact paths, never source or generated rows or mapping literals. An enabled audit log adds one started/terminal record to every invocation, including otherwise read-only tools. Tool Reads Writes or other effects Review requirement profile_csv Selected CSV New safe aggregate profile JSON No generation approval; authorize profiling of the selected input. infer_dataset_spec Safe profile file or bounded inline profile New specification Proposal only; no generation. plan_dataset CSV, CSV folder, or safe profile New planning directory, profile, spec and plan artifacts Stops before generation for human review. plan_trino_dataset Bounded safe Trino profile payload New planning directory and spec/plan artifacts Stops for review; this tool makes no database connection. inspect_dataset_plan Existing plan, spec and completion artifacts None, apart from optional audit Read-only inspection; returns the current spec fingerprint. approve_dataset_plan Existing plan and exact current spec Synthetic output, validation, manifest, approval/completion artifacts Human must review and approve the exact reviewed_spec_sha256 first; stale fingerprints reject. recover_dataset_plan Existing interrupted plan and published bundle Recovery/completion artifacts Reuses the human-reviewed fingerprint; revalidates, never regenerates rows. generate_dataset Reviewed spec and embedded/file/inline business rules New synthetic bundle, validation and manifest Lower-level direct generation: no planning approval argument. Require client/operator approval before granting this call. export_dataset Reviewed spec and rules Fresh synthetic bundle in the requested format Same direct-generation review policy; not conversion/export of arbitrary source rows. validate_dataset Spec and generated bundle with matching manifest New report only when output_path is supplied No generation approval; omit output_path for inspection without a new report file. review_transformation Fixed local source, policy and referenced mappings None, apart from optional audit Review only; cannot issue a preservation receipt or execute. execute_transformation Exact reviewed local snapshot, policy/mappings and any required existing receipt New labelled mixed-origin bundle and temporary work Requires snapshot_sha256 ; preservation additionally needs a matching human local-CLI receipt. common_transformation Saved batch profile and its local inputs/policies/mappings review : no retained output; validate : temporary output; execute : temporary output or new selected destination Validate/execute bind the exact digest; preservation consumes an existing local receipt. Cannot issue approval. configured_query_session Batch profile, bounded SQL references and configured database on open ; frozen captures afterward Owned temporary captures; execute publishes selected output; close , expiry and shutdown clean up open needs separate database authority. Validate/execute bind the digest; preservation consumes local approval. Review/validate/execute never reconnect. The generator console entrypoint injects a workspace and session owner and registers all 14 tools above. The module-level SDK object has only the 12 base tools; common_transformation and configured_query_session need explicit runtime ownership when embedded. Do not use a shorter SDK inventory as the console server's permission list. The two extensions retain their separate activation/release acceptance gates; registration or a documentation example does not authorize private data access. See the transformation and SQL-session workflow . Synthetic planning approval and preservation approval are different contracts. The synthetic workflow checks a reviewed spec fingerprint and writes its own generation receipt; it cannot prove that a human actually read the spec. The client must obtain that review before calling approval. Advanced direct generation tools do not enforce this planning sequence. Do not automatically allow them to bypass the review-first client policy. Resuming an existing client conversation adds no rights. Restore its existing workspace, installation, connection and narrow tool policy, then inspect the saved plan and review the full current specification before new dataset consent. Client tool prompts, operating-system access and dataset review remain separate; an earlier consent phrase or successful resume preflight does not establish current-specification review. Preservation receipts must be issued by the separate human local CLI through its controlling terminal. MCP has no preservation approval tool or approved boolean. A hash, tool-call confirmation or database grant cannot replace the matching receipt. Changed source/policy/mapping bytes invalidate it. Explicit mapped replacement retains its separate reviewed contract and is not an implicit preservation or source-copy fallback. Trino Tool Rights ¶ The default aggregate-only tools return metadata and aggregates. The explicit opt-in run_safe_select is a separate row-returning surface with different disclosure risks and is unnecessary for planning synthetic data. Give the Trino identity only the metadata visibility and SELECT access needed for the selected dataset. Configure grants in the actual Trino access-control system and underlying connector; there is no universal GRANT script for every backend. None of these tools needs DDL, DML, ownership, role administration or grant-option rights. Database grants remain necessary even when application allowlists are configured. Tool Database work Response / additional permission list_catalogs Catalog discovery Only catalog names admitted by the catalog allowlist. list_schemas Schema discovery in an allowed catalog Only schema names admitted by the schema allowlist. list_tables Table discovery in an allowed catalog/schema Table names visible to the database identity; column selectors do not filter this list. describe_table Column metadata in an allowed catalog/schema Visible column names/types; column selectors do not filter this response. profile_table Aggregate count for one table Count only. profile_column Cardinality/null aggregates for one column Aggregate counts, not source rows. profile_table_safe Selected column profiles and table count Bounded aggregate profile, synthetic category labels/masked patterns; no source rows. profile_foreign_key Parent/child key relationship aggregates Counts/confidence; needs read access to both tables and key columns. profile_temporal_ordering Ordering aggregates Counts/confidence; needs both temporal columns. profile_formula_rule Formula residual aggregates Counts/confidence; needs target and all operand columns. profile_conditional_required Conditional null-check aggregates Counts/confidence; needs condition and target columns. profile_conditional_allowed_values Conditional membership aggregates Counts/confidence; use only reviewed non-sensitive rule literals. profile_aggregate_mapping Parent/child aggregate comparison Counts/confidence; needs both tables, keys and measure columns. run_safe_select Bounded validated read-only SELECT Optional row-returning tool , absent unless TRINO_ENABLE_SAFE_SELECT=true . Strings and recognized sensitive values are masked; other source values may remain. Never use its rows as generated data or relay them to an LLM. TRINO_ALLOWED_CATALOGS and TRINO_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS are required by default. They are independent sets, not catalog/schema pairs: with two values in each, each catalog can admit both schemas. Use narrow values and database grants when different catalogs require different access. TRINO_ALLOWED_TABLE_COLUMNS narrows column selection for profile_table_safe . It is not a universal per-tool ACL : metadata discovery, count/cardinality tools, rule probes and optional run_safe_select do not enforce these selectors. The optional row tool checks catalog/schema scope and SQL safety, not this column list. Enforce strict table/column visibility through the database identity, and limit callable tools in the client. Table-qualified catalog.schema.table.* expands bounded metadata for safe profiling; it is not an unrestricted SQL projection or permission to disclose raw categories. Default aggregate profiling substitutes synthetic category labels or masked patterns. Raw category queries are internal bounded work, not row disclosure. For example, these application settings select two columns for safe table profiling; the database administrator must separately restrict the reader: { "TRINO_ALLOWED_CATALOGS": "hive", "TRINO_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS": "test_data", "TRINO_ALLOWED_TABLE_COLUMNS": "hive.test_data.customers.customer_id,hive.test_data.customers.status", "TRINO_ENABLE_SAFE_SELECT": "false" } Place these values in the Trino server's env alongside its verified HTTPS endpoint and runtime authentication settings, as shown in client configuration . Missing/denied rights should be resolved by narrowing the request or having the administrator grant the selected read access, not by enabling TRINO_ALLOW_UNRESTRICTED or TRINO_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP . See configuration for authentication and invocation limits ; a larger budget does not grant access to more data. Choose A Client Policy And Check It ¶ For the review-first synthetic workflow, enable plan_dataset (or plan_trino_dataset ) and inspect_dataset_plan ; require explicit human review before approve_dataset_plan . Allow recover_dataset_plan only with that same reviewed fingerprint and the recovery state reported by inspection. Add profile_csv , infer_dataset_spec , validate_dataset and direct generation only as the workflow needs them. Keep transformation and optional row tools outside a synthetic-only client's callable set. Apply these choices using the client's supported settings; the table is not a server configuration format. Before using the connection: Check the installed package version and tools/list ; compare names with the tables, including startup-only and optional tools. With a fictional fixture, run the planning/inspection/approval quickstart . Confirm no generated dataset exists before approval and outputs stay inside the selected workspace. For an independently authorized database, verify discovery and safe profiling using its restricted reader. Confirm an excluded catalog/schema is refused; do not infer table/column isolation from the column-selector setting alone. Confirm default Trino discovery omits run_safe_select ; verify only summaries and artifact paths reach the assistant. Keep credentials and raw files out of chat, prompts and committed client configuration. If a tool is missing, check version, installed extras, runtime composition and client tool policy. For filesystem refusal, check the narrow root, existing destination and process ownership. For database refusal, check both allowlists and database grants. Audit admission and resource-budget refusals require their own fixes; they are not permission to expand data access. See audit setup and the MCP recovery guide . The assistant client itself may use an external model provider under its own policy. These MCP servers do not need OpenAI/GigaChat API credentials for the workflows above and expose no advisor tool. Provider integration, shell/CLI access and arbitrary file-reading tools are separate capabilities with their own permissions; enabling MCP does not grant or constrain them. The finite stable 1.6.0 campaign completed with recorded coverage and limits . Candidate 1.7.0rc1 has separate installed-interface evidence . The acceptance matrix also contains historical and remaining targets; it does not establish new live database, client UI, preservation approval or all-route capacity acceptance.
